=== NOTES 2:53 | Inter-state Relations – Inter-state Council, Zonal Councils, River-water Disputes (article 262), Full Faith and Credit
## SUB 0 | Inter-State Council – Article 263
[53:0:0] # Article 263 and who sets it up
[53:0:1] - **Article 263** = provision for an **Inter-State Council** to effect co-ordination **between the States** and **between the Centre and the States** (not Arts. 260, 261, 262, 264, 360, 365 or 368). Art. 262 is river-water disputes; Art. 261 is full faith and credit.
[53:0:2] - Set up by **the President** by order, when public interest would be served (not Parliament, the PM, the Council of Ministers, the Speaker, the NDC or a Zonal Council); the President also defines its duties, organisation and procedure.
[53:0:3] - Art. 263 duties: (a) **enquire into and advise upon disputes** between States; (b) **investigate and discuss subjects of common interest**; (c) make **recommendations for better co-ordination of policy and action**.
[53:0:4] - Other councils set up under Art. 263: **Central Council of Health** (and Family Welfare), **Central Council of Local Self-Government** (1954), **Transport Development Council**, Regional Councils for Sales Tax.
[53:0:5] # Establishment (1990)
[53:0:6] - Set up by **Presidential order of 28 May 1990** (V.P. Singh government) on the recommendation of the **Sarkaria Commission**, which made a strong case for a permanent council called the "**Inter-Governmental Council**".
[53:0:7] - Earlier backers: **First ARC (1966-69)** and the **Rajamannar Committee (1969)** – but neither got it set up.
[53:0:8] - Sarkaria also proposed constitutional status under **Art. 263** for the NDC renamed as the **National Economic and Development Council**.
[53:0:9] - **Nature:** a **constitutional, recommendatory** body for consultation – advice **not binding**, not a court (Art. 131 disputes go to the Supreme Court).
[53:0:10] - **Meetings:** at least **three a year** (on paper), held **in camera**; all questions decided by **consensus** (not by simple, two-thirds or three-fourths majority). Only **11 meetings** so far, the last on **16 July 2016**.
[53:0:11] # Composition
[53:0:12] TABLE head: Post | Holder
  [53:0:12.0] Chairman | Prime Minister (not the President)
  [53:0:12.1] Members | Chief Ministers of all States and of UTs with legislatures
  [53:0:12.2] Members | Administrators of UTs without assemblies
  [53:0:12.3] Members (only then) | Governors of States under President's Rule – not permanent members for all States
  [53:0:12.4] Members | Six Union Cabinet ministers (incl. Home Minister) nominated by the PM
  [53:0:12.5] Permanent invitees | Five Cabinet ministers / MoS (independent charge) nominated by the PM
  [53:0:12.6] Standing Committee (1996) | Chaired by the Union Home Minister; 5 Union ministers + 9 CMs – reconstituted November 2024 with Amit Shah as chairperson
  [53:0:12.7] Secretariat | Inter-State Council Secretariat, set up 1991, headed by a Secretary to GoI; since 2011 also the secretariat of the Zonal Councils
[53:0:13] > Statement trap: "set up on Rajamannar's recommendation", "chaired by the President" and "recommendations binding" are all wrong; the **Secretariat (1991; Zonal Councils since 2011)** statement is the correct one.
[53:0:14] > A–R: Art. 263 contemplates the Council (true). Rajamannar did urge it "immediately" (true) – but a 1969 committee cannot explain a 1950 Article, and the body actually came on **Sarkaria's** case.
[53:0:15] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams (nextgen-polity-full) p.311, p.315-316; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.16 p.251-254; PIB (ISC reconstitution, Nov 2024)
## SUB 1 | Zonal Councils and the North Eastern Council
[53:1:0] # Zonal Councils
[53:1:1] - **Statutory, not constitutional** bodies – set up by **Parliament** under the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956** (Sections 15-22); idea of **PM Jawaharlal Nehru**. "Regional councils are constituted by **Parliamentary laws**."
[53:1:2] - States and UTs grouped with an advisory council each = **Zonal Council** (not State, Regional or Joint Council).
[53:1:3] - **Five** zonal councils: **Northern, Central, Eastern, Western, Southern**. **Chandigarh**, though not a State, is in the Northern council.
[53:1:4] - **Chairman:** the **Union Home Minister** – common chairman of all five (not the PM). **Vice-Chairman:** a **CM by annual rotation**.
[53:1:5] - Members: Home Minister, **CMs of the zone's States**, **two other ministers from each State**, **Administrators of UTs**; advisers (no vote): a NITI Aayog nominee, Chief Secretaries, Development Commissioners.
[53:1:6] - Only **deliberative and advisory** bodies – recommendations **not binding**; described as **sub-federal links** that promote **co-operation and integration** among States (both statements true).
[53:1:7] - Objectives: **emotional integration**, check **regionalism, linguism**, remove after-effects of reorganisation, co-operate on development projects, **political equilibrium** between regions.
[53:1:8] TABLE head: Zonal Council | Members | HQ
  [53:1:8.0] Northern | HP, Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, Delhi, Chandigarh, J&K, Ladakh | New Delhi
  [53:1:8.1] Central | UP, Uttarakhand, Chhattisgarh, MP | Prayagraj
  [53:1:8.2] Eastern | Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha | Kolkata
  [53:1:8.3] Western | Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, DNH and Daman & Diu | Mumbai
  [53:1:8.4] Southern | Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Puducherry | Chennai
[53:1:9] # Southern Zonal Council meetings
[53:1:10] - **27th meeting – Thiruvananthapuram, 28 December 2016** – chaired by Union Home Minister **Rajnath Singh** (not CM Pinarayi Vijayan, Arun Jaitley or Kiran Bedi).
[53:1:11] - **29th meeting – Tirupati**, chaired by **Amit Shah**.
[53:1:12] - **31st meeting – 20 August 2026, Tamil Nadu**: Amit Shah urged early settlement of southern water disputes; Telangana sought national status for **Kaleshwaram** and **Palamuru-Rangareddy**.
[53:1:13] # North Eastern Council
[53:1:14] - Separate statute: **North Eastern Council Act, 1971** (came into existence 8 August 1972) – statutory, not under Art. 263.
[53:1:15] - **2002 amendment:** **Sikkim** added as the **8th** member → the North Eastern zone/council now has **8 States** (Assam, Arunachal, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura, Sikkim); NEC became a **regional planning body**.
[53:1:16] - Composition after the 2002 Act: **Governors** and **Chief Ministers** of the 8 States + **three members nominated by the President** (the Home Minister is not a member under the Act; he chairs it since 2018 by Cabinet decision; DoNER Minister vice-chairman).
[53:1:17] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams (nextgen-polity-full) p.317-318; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.16 p.255-258; NEC (Amendment) Act 2002 (UPSC CSE 2024 key); PIB (27th SZC, 28 Dec 2016)
## SUB 2 | Constitutional, Statutory and Extra-constitutional Bodies
[53:2:0] TABLE head: Body | Status | Basis
  [53:2:0.0] Inter-State Council | Constitutional | Art. 263 (Presidential order 1990)
  [53:2:0.1] River water tribunals | Statutory | ISRWD Act, 1956 (under Art. 262)
  [53:2:0.2] Zonal Councils | Statutory | States Reorganisation Act, 1956
  [53:2:0.3] North Eastern Council | Statutory | NEC Act, 1971
  [53:2:0.4] National Security Council | Executive (non-statutory) | Government order, 1998
  [53:2:0.5] NDC, Governors' Conference, Planning Commission, NITI Aayog | Extra-constitutional and extra-legal | Executive resolution / convention
[53:2:1] - "Constitutional body concerned with inter-State relations" = **Inter-State Council** – not the NDC, Planning Commission, NITI Aayog, river tribunals or Zonal Councils.
[53:2:2] - **UPSC 2025:** of ISC, NSC and Zonal Councils, **only one** (ISC) was established as per the Constitution.
[53:2:3] - **UPSC 1995:** extra-constitutional **and** extra-legal devices = **NDC and Governors' Conference** only (Zonal Councils have a law behind them; ISC is in the Constitution).
[53:2:4] - Zonal Council "**is a constitutional body**" = the feature that is NOT true.
[53:2:5] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.16 p.253, p.255; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams p.317; UPSC CSE 2025 key
## SUB 3 | Full Faith and Credit (Art. 261) and Inter-State Trade (Arts. 301-307)
[53:3:0] # Article 261
[53:3:1] - **261(1):** **full faith and credit** throughout India to **public acts, records and judicial proceedings** of the **Union and every State** (not Arts. 133, 142, 256, 263, 266 or 324).
[53:3:2] - **261(2):** manner of proof and their effect – decided by **Parliament by law**.
[53:3:3] - **261(3):** **final judgments or orders of civil courts** can be **executed anywhere** in India (civil only, not criminal).
[53:3:4] - Modelled on the **US** Full Faith and Credit Clause.
[53:3:5] # Articles 301-307 (Part XIII)
[53:3:6] TABLE head: Article | Content
  [53:3:6.0] 301 | Trade, commerce and intercourse throughout India shall be free (inter- and intra-State) – not Arts. 19, 25, 299, 300, 308 or 309
  [53:3:6.1] 302 | Parliament may restrict it in public interest
  [53:3:6.2] 303 | No preference or discrimination between States (except scarcity)
  [53:3:6.3] 304(b) | State may impose reasonable restrictions – the bill needs the previous sanction of the President (not the Governor, Union government, PM, CM or ISC)
  [53:3:6.4] 305 | Saves existing laws and laws for State monopolies
  [53:3:6.5] 306 | Part B States – repealed
  [53:3:6.6] 307 | Parliament may appoint an authority (Inter-State Trade and Commerce Commission) – none appointed so far
[53:3:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams p.311, p.316-317; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.16 p.254-255
## SUB 4 | River Water Disputes – Article 262 and Tribunals
[53:4:0] - **Art. 262(1):** Parliament may provide for **adjudication** of disputes on the **use, distribution or control of waters of inter-State rivers** (not Arts. 56, 105 or 352).
[53:4:1] - **Art. 262(2):** Parliament may bar the **Supreme Court and all other courts**; so **Art. 131** (SC original jurisdiction over Centre-State disputes) does not cover water disputes.
[53:4:2] - **Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956:** Centre sets up an **ad hoc tribunal**; a State complains to the **Central Government** (Section 3); award final and binding.
[53:4:3] - **River Boards Act, 1956** (**not 1970**) – boards to advise States; **no board ever set up** under it. National Water Policy: 1987.
[53:4:4] - **Jurisdiction:** water is a **State** subject (Entry 17, List II) but **Parliament** regulates inter-State rivers when declared expedient in public interest (Entry 56, List I).
[53:4:5] - A downstream State **cannot** build a dam that **submerges an upstream State's territory** without its consent – the false statement.
[53:4:6] TABLE head: Tribunal | Set up | States
  [53:4:6.0] Krishna (KWDT-I) | 1969 | Maharashtra, Karnataka, AP
  [53:4:6.1] Godavari | 1969 | Maharashtra, Karnataka, AP, MP, Odisha
  [53:4:6.2] Narmada | 1969 | Rajasthan, Gujarat, MP, Maharashtra (not Karnataka)
  [53:4:6.3] Ravi and Beas | 1986 | Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan
  [53:4:6.4] Cauvery | 1990 | Karnataka, Kerala, TN, Puducherry
  [53:4:6.5] Krishna (KWDT-II) | 2004 | Maharashtra, Karnataka, AP
  [53:4:6.6] Vansadhara | 2010 | Odisha and AP
  [53:4:6.7] Mahadayi | 2010 | Goa, Karnataka, Maharashtra
  [53:4:6.8] Mahanadi | 2018 | Odisha, Chhattisgarh
[53:4:7] - Tribunals involving AP: **Godavari, Krishna (I and II), Vansadhara**.
[53:4:8] - **Mullaperiyar** dam (1895, Periyar) is in **Kerala** but run by **Tamil Nadu** under a lease.
[53:4:9] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams p.314-315; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.16 p.251-253; Constitution, Seventh Schedule
## SUB 5 | Krishna and Godavari – AP Reorganisation Act, 2014
[53:5:0] - **KRMB** and **GRMB** set up under the **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014**, supervised by an **Apex Council** (Union Water Resources Minister + the two CMs).
[53:5:1] - **Apex Council functions (s.84):** supervise the boards; **plan and approve proposals for new projects**; **resolve disputes amicably**; **refer disputes not covered by KWDT** to a tribunal under the ISRWD Act, 1956. It does **not** take barrage matters **directly to the Supreme Court**.
[53:5:2] - **Section 89:** the **KWDT (KWDT-II)** term extended to make **project-wise allocation** and to prepare an **operational protocol for project-wise release of water in deficit years** – the Tribunal, not the boards or the States.
[53:5:3] - KWDT-II term: **two years from 1.8.2014**, then extended **one year at a time** (from **1.8.2016**, 1.8.2017, …).
[53:5:4] - KWDT-I allotted **811 tmcft** to undivided AP; ad hoc split from 2014-15 **512 (AP) : 299 (Telangana)** (66:34).
[53:5:5] - Centre set fresh terms of reference for KWDT-II on the AP-Telangana dispute in **October 2023**.
[53:5:6] - **Jan 2026 (CWC-chaired inter-State committee):** AP rejected Telangana's **50:50** Krishna demand as **contrary to the KWDT awards and Apex Council decisions**; objected to 968 tmcft of Godavari water claimed for Telangana projects.
[53:5:7] ~~ Sources: AP Reorganisation Act 2014, ss.84-89 (indiacode.nic.in); PIB, MoWR release (KWDT-II extensions, PRID 1542169); app notes 2:53

=== NOTES 2:55 | Rajamannar Committee (1969) – Appointment and Recommendations
## SUB 0 | Rajamannar Committee – Appointment and Purpose
[55:0:0] TABLE head: Item | Detail
  [55:0:0.0] Formal name | Centre-State Relations Inquiry Committee
  [55:0:0.1] Appointed by | Tamil Nadu – DMK government of M. Karunanidhi (not the Centre)
  [55:0:0.2] Year | 1969 (22 Sept); report 1971
  [55:0:0.3] Chairman | Dr P.V. Rajamannar, former Chief Justice of the Madras High Court
  [55:0:0.4] Members | Three in all – Rajamannar, A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar, P. Chandra Reddy
[55:0:1] - **First** committee on Centre-State relations appointed by a **State**.
[55:0:2] - Purpose: to **study the Centre-State relations** as a whole and suggest amendments to secure **utmost autonomy to the States** (not Tamil Nadu's relations with the Centre or with other southern States, nor UT-State relations).
[55:0:3] - Took forward **C.N. Annadurai's 1967** view that the Union need not control **education and health**; it was to reduce, not strengthen, the Centre's control over them.
[55:0:4] - P.V. Rajamannar also chaired the **4th Finance Commission**.
[55:0:5] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.15 p.237-238; app notes 2:55
## SUB 1 | Rajamannar Recommendations
[55:1:0] TABLE head: Subject | Rajamannar recommended
  [55:1:0.0] Inter-State Council | Set up immediately under Art. 263; no decision affecting States without consulting it; every Bill affecting States to be referred to it first
  [55:1:0.1] Article 356 | Complete deletion (with 357 and 365); if kept, only for a complete breakdown
  [55:1:0.2] All-India Services | Abolish IAS, IPS (and IFoS) – to reduce central administrative control
  [55:1:0.3] Planning Commission | Abolish – extra-constitutional; alone decided grants to States; replace with a statutory body
  [55:1:0.4] Finance Commission | Make permanent; revitalise with wider revenue devolution
  [55:1:0.5] Governor | Delete "pleasure of the Governor" clause for the State ministry – not strengthen the Governor system
[55:1:1] - Ending IAS and IPS = **Rajamannar** (UPSC 1993) – not the Dhebar, Kalelkar or Kher commissions, nor Sarkaria.
[55:1:2] - Passage clue: "made a call for **immediate constitution of the Inter-State Council**, every Bill affecting States referred to it first, Art. 356 only in rare cases" = **Rajamannar**.
[55:1:3] - Passage clue: "greater autonomy in legislative and fiscal matters, critical analysis of the '**strong Centre**' concept, States' competence to amend Central laws, mandatory consultation" = **Rajamannar** (Sarkaria **defended** a strong Centre).
[55:1:4] # Findings
[55:1:5] - Despite the federal form, States had become "**administrative units of the Centre**"; causes – special central powers, **one-party rule**, weak State finances, **central planning**.
[55:1:6] - Overreach Articles: **256, 257, 365** (not 280, 282).
[55:1:7] - The Centre's control over States in the **planning process** has been termed "**municipal relations**" (UPSC 1994) – not legislative, administrative or financial control.
[55:1:8] - Relations depend on constitutional provisions, conventions and practices, judicial interpretation and mechanisms for dialogue.
[55:1:9] # Seventh Schedule and residuary powers
[55:1:10] - Transfer subjects (e.g. **stock exchanges, oil fields, trade unions, industrial disputes**, inland waterways) from Union/Concurrent Lists to the **State List** – **not foreign affairs**.
[55:1:11] - **Residuary powers → States** (Sarkaria: residuary taxation with Parliament, other residuary to the Concurrent List).
[55:1:12] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.15 p.237-238; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams p.313; app notes 2:55
## SUB 2 | Aftermath and Influence
[55:2:0] - **Centre ignored** the report; no action.
[55:2:1] - **April 1974:** TN Assembly adopted a **State autonomy resolution** based on it.
[55:2:2] - DMK slogan: "**autonomy for the States, federalism at the Centre**".
[55:2:3] - Base for **Anandpur Sahib (1973)** and the **West Bengal memorandum (1977)**.
[55:2:4] - The ISC (1990) came through **Sarkaria**, not Rajamannar.
[55:2:5] - **Kurian Joseph Committee** – appointed by Tamil Nadu in **2025** (Part I, 16 Feb 2026): State (1969) → Centre (1983, 2007) → State (2025).
[55:2:6] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.15 p.238; app notes 2:55

=== NOTES 2:56 | Sarkaria Commission (1983) – Recommendations on Legislative, Administrative and Financial Relations
## SUB 0 | Sarkaria Commission at a Glance
[56:0:0] TABLE head: Item | Detail
  [56:0:0.0] Set up by | Central Government, 9 June 1983 (Indira Gandhi government)
  [56:0:0.1] Chairman | Justice Rajinder (Ranjit) Singh Sarkaria, retired Supreme Court judge
  [56:0:0.2] Members | B. Sivaraman and Dr S.R. Sen – 3 in all (not Rajamannar, Punchhi, V. Shankar, Hanumanthaiah)
  [56:0:0.3] Objective | Examine the relationship and balance of power between Centre and States; suggest changes within the existing constitutional framework
  [56:0:0.4] Report | January 1988 (worked 1983-87); 247 recommendations
[56:0:1] - Subject = **Centre-State relations** – not President-PM, legislature-executive, executive-judiciary, reservations, inter-State disputes or agricultural trade.
[56:0:2] - It **rejected** curtailing the Centre: a **strong Centre** is essential, but not centralisation ("blood pressure at the centre, anaemia at the periphery").
[56:0:3] - Report year: **1988** (a few keys, e.g. BPSC 2018, say 1987).
[56:0:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams p.313-314; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.15 p.238-240
## SUB 1 | Recommendations on the Governor
[56:1:0] - Governor should be an **eminent person** in some walk of life.
[56:1:1] - **From outside the State**; a **detached figure**, not intimately connected with local politics; **not taken part in politics in the recent past** (UPSC 2019: Sarkaria, not ARC, Rajamannar or NCRWC).
[56:1:2] - **Chief Minister** to be consulted; procedure to be in the Constitution.
[56:1:3] - **Secure 5-year term**, not disturbed except for **extremely compelling reasons** – the first body to recommend this.
[56:1:4] - Governor cannot dismiss a ministry that commands a majority; decide on **Bills within a specified period**.
[56:1:5] - Convention in practice: Governor is a **person from outside the State** (no age bar, not appointed by the CM, no legal qualification).
[56:1:6] - **NOT** recommended: Governor "should have **travelled extensively** in the State", "must be an eminent **political leader**", "should have **served the Government** long", "other-State person shall not be appointed".
[56:1:7] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.15 p.239-241; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams p.313
## SUB 2 | Inter-State Council and Article 356
[56:2:0] # Inter-Governmental Council
[56:2:1] - A **permanent Inter-State Council** called the **Inter-Governmental Council** under **Art. 263** – the main implemented recommendation; ISC set up **28 May 1990** (ISC Secretariat 1991).
[56:2:2] - "Establish an **Inter-Government Council in place of Inter-State Council**" = **Sarkaria** (not Rajamannar, Punchhi or the ARC).
[56:2:3] # Article 356
[56:2:4] - 1. Use **very sparingly**, in extreme cases, as a **last resort**, after a **warning** to the State.
[56:2:5] - 2. Doubt over majority → **floor test** in the Assembly, not the Governor's own assessment.
[56:2:6] - 3. **Hung Assembly** → invite parties in a **set order of preference**.
[56:2:7] - **A–R:** Sarkaria said use Art. 356 sparingly **because** parties in power at the Centre had **misused** it → both true, R explains A.
[56:2:8] - Courts relied on Sarkaria in **S.R. Bommai (1994)** and **Rameshwar Prasad (2006)**.
[56:2:9] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.15 p.239-240, ch.16 p.253; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams p.313-314
## SUB 3 | Legislative, Administrative and Financial Recommendations
[56:3:0] TABLE head: Sphere | Recommendation
  [56:3:0.0] Legislative | Consult the States (institutionalised process) before a law on a Concurrent List subject
  [56:3:0.1] Legislative | Residuary taxation stays with Parliament; other residuary powers to the Concurrent List
  [56:3:0.2] Administrative | Strengthen All-India Services and create more (Rajamannar: abolish)
  [56:3:0.3] Administrative | Centre may deploy central armed forces even without the State's request (consultation desirable)
  [56:3:0.4] Administrative | Zonal Councils constituted afresh and reactivated
  [56:3:0.5] Financial | Cesses and surcharges minimal, time-bound, then merged into the shareable pool
  [56:3:0.6] Financial | Present Finance Commission – Planning Commission division is reasonable; continue
  [56:3:0.7] Financial | NDC renamed National Economic and Development Council
  [56:3:0.8] Financial | Net proceeds of corporation tax permissibly shareable
[56:3:1] - Sarkaria = first official body to make **cooperative federalism** the guiding principle ("federalism is a functional arrangement for co-operative action").
[56:3:2] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.15 p.239-240; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams p.313-314
## SUB 4 | Implementation and Comparison
[56:4:0] - Of **247** recommendations, **180** accepted/implemented (65 not accepted, 2 under implementation).
[56:4:1] TABLE head: Body | By / year | Stance
  [56:4:1.0] Rajamannar | Tamil Nadu, 1969 | State autonomy; abolish AIS and Art. 356
  [56:4:1.1] Sarkaria | Centre, 1983 | Within the Constitution; strong Centre; strengthen AIS
  [56:4:1.2] Punchhi | Centre, 2007 | Localised emergency; fixed tenure for Governors
  [56:4:1.3] Kurian Joseph | Tamil Nadu, 2025 | Federal "structural reset"
[56:4:2] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.15 p.240; app notes 2:56

=== NOTES 2:57 | M.m. Punchhi Commission (2007) – Recommendations and Their Status
## SUB 0 | Punchhi Commission at a Glance
[57:0:0] TABLE head: Item | Detail
  [57:0:0.0] Formal name | Commission on Centre-State Relations – the Second such commission
  [57:0:0.1] Set up by | Government of India (UPA government), 27 April 2007
  [57:0:0.2] Chairman | Justice Madan Mohan Punchhi, former Chief Justice of India (not Sarkaria, B. Sivaraman or Venkatachaliah)
  [57:0:0.3] Members | Dhirendra Singh, Vinod Kumar Duggal, Dr N.R. Madhava Menon, Vijay Shanker
  [57:0:0.4] Report | March 2010, 7 volumes, 1,456 pages; 273 recommendations (Laxmikanth: "over 310")
[57:0:1] - **Mandate:** review Centre-State arrangements in the light of changes since the **Sarkaria Commission** – Panchayati Raj, economic reforms, coalition politics, internal security.
[57:0:2] - Conclusion: **cooperative federalism** is the key to unity and development.
[57:0:3] - Appointed **2007**, report **2010**. Order: Rajamannar **1969** → Sarkaria **1983** → Punchhi **2007**.
[57:0:4] - **Rajamannar** recommended an ISC consulted on matters of national importance; Sarkaria a permanent ISC; Punchhi a strengthened ISC.
[57:0:5] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.15 p.240-244; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams p.314
## SUB 1 | Recommendations on the Governor
[57:1:0] - **Fixed tenure of 5 years**; removal not at the sweet will of the Centre (Sarkaria first proposed a secure five-year term).
[57:1:1] - Follow **Sarkaria's guidelines**: eminent person, **from outside the State**, detached, not too active in politics.
[57:1:2] - Not in **active politics, even at the local level**, for **at least a couple of (two) years** before appointment.
[57:1:3] - **Article 156:** delete "**during the pleasure of the President**"; removal only by **impeachment by the State Legislature**, on the lines of the **President's impeachment**.
[57:1:4] - **Universities:** Governors should **not be Chancellors** or hold other **statutory positions** – role confined to constitutional provisions.
[57:1:5] - **Bills:** decide within **six months**; Art. 163 gives no general discretion.
[57:1:6] - **Hung assembly:** a **pre-poll alliance** is treated as **one political party**; then largest single party, post-poll coalitions.
[57:1:7] - Criticised **arbitrary dismissal** of Governors.
[57:1:8] - **Distractors** (not recommended): **periodic rotation** of Governors, **abolition** of the office, CM's **consent** (only consultation) for appointment.
[57:1:9] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.15 p.241-242; app notes 2:57
## SUB 2 | Articles 355 and 356 and Central Forces
[57:2:0] - **Amend Articles 355 and 356** – "no need to amend them" is the **wrong** statement.
[57:2:1] - **Art. 356** only as a **last resort**; incorporate **S.R. Bommai** guidelines.
[57:2:2] - **"Localised emergency":** the Centre takes over a **district or part of a district** for a **limited period** (under Art. 355), instead of a whole State.
[57:2:3] - **Central forces:** in **communal violence**, deploy **suo motu, without the State's consent, for a short period**; consent obtained afterwards.
[57:2:4] - **Article 357:** laws made by Parliament for a State under President's Rule **continue after the Proclamation ends** until changed by the State Legislature.
[57:2:5] - Origin of "either on their request or otherwise": the **First ARC**.
[57:2:6] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.15 p.242; app notes 2:57
## SUB 3 | Inter-State Council, NIC and Other Forums
[57:3:0] TABLE head: Forum | Punchhi recommendation
  [57:3:0.0] Inter-State Council (Art. 263) | Amend Art. 263 to make it credible; meet at least thrice a year; agenda in consultation with the States
  [57:3:0.1] National Integration Council | Meet at least once a year – "once in two years" is the wrong statement
  [57:3:0.2] Zonal Councils | Meet at least twice a year
  [57:3:0.3] National Water Resources Council | Bigger role
[57:3:1] - **Concurrent List:** reach **broad agreement with the States through the ISC** before legislating.
[57:3:2] - **New Union List entry:** **environment, ecology and climate change**.
[57:3:3] - **Art. 249:** Rajya Sabha resolution by **two-thirds present and voting**, national interest; valid **one year**, renewable; **101st Amendment (2016)** extended it to GST.
[57:3:4] - **PPP:** Punchhi **favoured** private participation in public services, distinguished PPP from privatisation, and wanted good-governance and DPSP principles applied to private players – "**private participation should be avoided**" is NOT its view.
[57:3:5] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.15 p.240-243; Punchhi Commission Report Vol. II-IV (interstate.gov.in); app notes 2:57
## SUB 4 | Financial Recommendations and Status
[57:4:0] - **Finance Commission and Planning Commission** to coordinate; periods **synchronised with the Five Year Plans**.
[57:4:1] - **Cesses and surcharges** to be **reviewed and limited**; States involved in FC terms of reference.
[57:4:2] - **16th Finance Commission:** **Arvind Panagariya**; 2026-31; vertical share kept at **41%**; no recommendation on cesses, a "grand bargain"; revised formula raises the share of southern States incl. **Andhra Pradesh**; divisible pool ~**81%** of gross tax (2025-26).
[57:4:3] TABLE head: Finance Commission | Chairman
  [57:4:3.0] 14th | Y.V. Reddy
  [57:4:3.1] 15th | N.K. Singh
  [57:4:3.2] 16th | Arvind Panagariya
[57:4:4] # Status
[57:4:5] - Report referred to the ISC; **11th ISC meeting (16 July 2016)** took it up; Standing Committee finished in 2017-18.
[57:4:6] - **Article 156 unchanged**; Governors still act as **Chancellors**.
[57:4:7] TABLE head: Case / opinion | Date | Held
  [57:4:7.0] State of Tamil Nadu v. Governor of Tamil Nadu | 8 April 2025 | Fixed timelines for Governors on Bills
  [57:4:7.1] Presidential Reference opinion | 20 Nov 2025 | No court-fixed timelines or "deemed assent"
[57:4:8] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.15 p.244; 16th FC report (fincomindia.nic.in); app notes 2:57

  [58:0:0.2] Committee of Governors | Bhagwan Sahay | Set up 1970, reported 1971 | President

[58:0:2] - "Commission under **Veerappa Moily**" = **Administrative Reforms** (UPSC 2008) – not police, tax or technical-education reform.
[58:0:3] - Sarkaria was the commission of the **Indira Gandhi** period – not M.C. Mehta, Malhotra (insurance) or Narasimham (banking).

## SUB 1 | First Administrative Reforms Commission (1966)
[58:1:0] - Six-member; set up a **study team on Centre-State relations** under **M.C. Setalvad**; report **1969** with **22 recommendations**.
[58:1:1] - Asked for an **Inter-State Council under Article 263** (1969); Governors with long public life and **non-partisan** attitude; maximum delegation and more resources to States.
[58:1:2] - Deploy central armed forces in States "**either on their request or otherwise**".
[58:1:3] - Also: **no political interference** in administration (civil-service neutrality).
[58:1:4] - **No action** was taken on its recommendations.
[58:1:5] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.15 p.237; app notes 2:58
## SUB 2 | Sarkaria and the Inter-Governmental Council
[58:2:0] - Sarkaria Commission **appointed 1983** (report 1988).
[58:2:1] - Recommended a **permanent Inter-State Council called the Inter-Governmental Council** under **Art. 263** – the only recommendation that became an institution: **Inter-State Council, 1990**.
[58:2:2] - Sarkaria = first to recommend **cooperative federalism** as the guiding principle (not Rajamannar, NCRWC or Punchhi).
[58:2:3] - **Chronology:** First ARC (1969) → Sarkaria (1983-88) → ISC (1990) → Punchhi (2007-10).
[58:2:4] - **Standing Committee of the ISC** (1996) is chaired by the **Union Home Minister**; it finished discussing all **273 Punchhi** recommendations in **May 2018**.
[58:2:5] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.16 p.253-254; app notes 2:58
## SUB 3 | NCRWC – Venkatachaliah Commission
[58:3:0] - **Constitutional Review Commission**, set up **February 2000** (Vajpayee govt), chaired by **M.N. Venkatachaliah**; reviewed the first 50 years incl. **social justice**; report **2002**.
[58:3:1] - **Centre-State chapter:** greater **fiscal autonomy for States**; **safeguards against misuse of Art. 356** (not deletion); Governor appointed after consulting the CM; **Inter-State Trade and Commerce Commission**.
[58:3:2] - **Judiciary:** **All India Judicial Service** and a **National Judicial Commission**.
[58:3:3] - **Elections:** nearly **two-thirds (~70%)** of elected representatives win with **less than 50%** of votes cast; examine a **50% + 1** rule.
[58:3:4] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.90 p.866-874; app notes 2:58
## SUB 4 | Second Administrative Reforms Commission
[58:4:0] - Constituted **31 August 2005** as a **Commission of Inquiry**, chairman **Veerappa Moily** (V. Ramachandran from 2009); **15 reports, 2006-2009**; the "**Bible**" of administrative reforms.
[58:4:1] - Key recommendations: **Code of Ethics**, **Right to Public Services** laws, **Department of E-Governance**, financial autonomy for PRIs and ULBs; a **National Judicial Council**.

=== NOTES 2:59 | Cooperative and Competitive Federalism – Niti Aayog, Gst Council, State Rankings
## SUB 0 | Cooperative, Competitive and Sub-federalism
[59:0:0] TABLE head: Type | Meaning
  [59:0:0.0] Federalism | Sharing of power between the Union and the States (not communism, fascism, oligarchy)
  [59:0:0.1] Cooperative federalism | Centre and States work together on a common platform; NITI's bottom-up version – "marble-cake federalism"
  [59:0:0.2] Competitive federalism | States compete with each other and with the Centre to draw investment and improve outcomes – e.g. comparing States on ease of doing business
  [59:0:0.3] Competitive sub-federalism | Local bodies compete with local bodies (districts, cities) – e.g. Aspirational Districts rankings
[59:0:1] - Cooperative federalism **first recommended by the Sarkaria Commission**; put into practice by **NITI Aayog (2015)**, whose **thrust is to promote cooperative federalism** (not just inclusive growth or correcting the planning process).
[59:0:2] - NITI planning: credible **village-level plans aggregated upwards**.
[59:0:3] - Competitive federalism fosters **competition among States to improve social and environmental outcomes** – the link to **sustainable development** (SDG India Index).
[59:0:4] - **GST Council** = cooperative; **NITI State rankings** = competitive.
[59:0:5] TABLE head: Label | Scholar
  [59:0:5.0] Cooperative federalism | Granville Austin
  [59:0:5.1] Bargaining federalism | Morris-Jones
  [59:0:5.2] Quasi-federal | K.C. Wheare
  [59:0:5.3] Federation with a centralising tendency | Ivor Jennings
[59:0:6] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.14 and ch.56; NextGen Polity; app notes 2:59
## SUB 1 | NITI Aayog, Planning Commission and NDC
[59:1:0] TABLE head: Body | Created by | Year | Status
  [59:1:0.0] Planning Commission | Cabinet resolution (non-statutory) | 1950 | Extra-constitutional; replaced by NITI
  [59:1:0.1] NDC | Executive resolution | 1952 | Highest body to approve Five Year Plans; role taken by NITI's Governing Council
  [59:1:0.2] NITI Aayog | Union Cabinet resolution | 1 January 2015 (not 2014) | Non-constitutional, non-statutory think-tank; no power to allocate plan grants
[59:1:1] - **Constitutional** body = directly established by the Constitution (EC, FC, CAG, PSCs); **statutory** = by Act (NHRC, **Lokpal**, NGT); the Planning Commission was **not** statutory.
[59:1:2] TABLE head: Post | Who
  [59:1:2.0] Chairperson | Prime Minister
  [59:1:2.1] Vice-Chairperson | Appointed by the PM (not the President); Ashok Kumar Lahiri (April 2026)
  [59:1:2.2] CEO | Secretary-rank officer, fixed tenure
  [59:1:2.3] Governing Council | PM + CMs of all States and of UTs with legislatures (Delhi, J&K, Puducherry) + Lt Governors of other UTs; first constituted Feb 2015; took over the NDC's role
  [59:1:2.4] Regional Councils | For issues affecting more than one State; formed for a specified tenure; jointly headed by a CM by rotation and a Union Minister
[59:1:3] - **Team India Hub** – State engagement; **Knowledge and Innovation Hub**; **DMEO** – monitoring and evaluation; **State Support Mission** – State Institutions for Transformation (GRIT Gujarat, **MITRA Maharashtra**).
[59:1:4] - **11th Governing Council meeting: 11 June 2026** – Swarna Andhra @2047 presented.
[59:1:5] # CM sub-groups (2015)
[59:1:6] TABLE head: Sub-group | Convener
  [59:1:6.0] Rationalisation of CSS (core of the core, core, optional) | Shivraj Singh Chouhan
  [59:1:6.1] Skill Development | Parkash Singh Badal
  [59:1:6.2] Swachh Bharat | N. Chandrababu Naidu
[59:1:7] - CM committee on **digital payments (2016)**: **Naidu**.
[59:1:8] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.56 (NITI Aayog); NITI Aayog resolution 1 Jan 2015; app notes 2:59

=== NOTES 2:60 | Devolution of Powers and Finances to Local Levels – Finance Commission and State Finance Commission Transfers
## SUB 0 | State Finance Commission – Article 243I
[60:0:0] # The body
[60:0:1] - **Art. 243I (Panchayats) / 243Y (Municipalities):** the **Governor** constitutes a **Finance Commission** within one year of the 73rd Amendment (1992) and then **every five years** to **review the financial position of the Panchayats** – not the President, Parliament, the Finance Ministry or the Chief Minister.
[60:0:2] - It is a **constitutional body** (Part IX, 73rd Amendment) – not informal, administrative or a "finance committee"/"advisory commission".
[60:0:3] - **243Y:** the **same SFC** also reviews the finances of **Municipalities**.
[60:0:4] # What it recommends to the Governor
[60:0:5] - **Principles governing** (a) the **distribution between the State and the Panchayats** of the net proceeds of State taxes, duties, tolls and fees, and their **allocation among Panchayats at all levels**; (b) the **determination of taxes, duties, tolls and fees that may be assigned to or appropriated by the Panchayats**; (c) **grants-in-aid** from the **Consolidated Fund of the State**.
[60:0:6] - Also **measures to improve the finances** of the Panchayats and any matter the **Governor** refers.
[60:0:7] - The **State Legislature** fixes its composition and members' qualifications; the **Governor lays the report, with an explanatory memorandum (action taken), before the State Legislature**.
[60:0:8] - So the SFC – not the Governor, the CM, the District Planning Committee or the State PR Ministry – is the body for **revenue distribution between the State and its local governments**.
[60:0:9] TABLE head: Article | Provision
  [60:0:9.0] 243G / 243W | Powers and functions – Eleventh Schedule (29) / Twelfth (18) – State "may" devolve
  [60:0:9.1] 243H / 243X | Panchayat/Municipal taxes, duties, tolls, fees – only if the State Legislature authorises; grants from the State Consolidated Fund
  [60:0:9.2] 243I / 243Y | State Finance Commission – Governor, every 5 years
  [60:0:9.3] 243J / 243Z | Maintenance and audit of accounts – by State law
  [60:0:9.4] 243K / 243ZA | State Election Commission
  [60:0:9.5] 243D | Reservation of seats
[60:0:10] # Andhra Pradesh SFCs
[60:0:11] TABLE head: SFC | Chair | Remember
  [60:0:11.0] 4th SFC | Prof. G. Nancharaiah | Report 30 Oct 2019; first after bifurcation
  [60:0:11.1] 5th SFC (2025-30) | Prof. S. Rathna Kumari | Report Dec 2024 to the Governor; extra help to local bodies with low per capita income; State matching grants to Central FC grants
[60:0:12] > Asked as: Article (243I – not 243H/243D/243J); appointed by (Governor); interval (5 years); constitutional status; which body recommends principles of taxes appropriated by Panchayats (SFC – UPSC 2010, asked twice); who reviews Panchayat finances / distributes revenue between State and local bodies.
[60:0:13] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch39 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.105 and p.114 (Art. 243-I); NextGen Polity APPSC Part 18.1 (src/polity/nextgen-polity-appsc-26.txt) p.10; app notes 2:60 sub 1-2
## SUB 1 | Fourteenth Finance Commission (2015-20) – Grants to Local Bodies
[60:1:0] # The design
[60:1:1] - **14th FC (Y.V. Reddy):** total local-body grant **₹2,87,436 crore** for 2015-20, of which **Panchayats ₹2,00,292 crore**, the rest to municipalities.
[60:1:2] - Grants only to **duly constituted** bodies and, among Panchayats, **only to Gram Panchayats** – the grant goes **directly to the GPs** (no share for block and district Panchayats; States do not decide a share for other tiers).
[60:1:3] - **Inter-State distribution of the grant:** **2011 population 90% : area 10%**.
[60:1:4] - **Within a State:** among GPs by the **latest SFC formula**; if none, **population 90 : area 10**.
[60:1:5] - **Basic : performance grant** – **Gram Panchayats 90 : 10**; **Municipalities 80 : 20**. Performance grant from **2016-17**, needs **audited accounts** and **increase in own revenue**.
[60:1:6] - **Undisbursed performance grant:** distributed on an **equitable basis among all the eligible Gram Panchayats** (not rolled over).
[60:1:7] - **Release:** States must pass the grant to the local bodies **within 15 days** of its credit to the State's account; for any delay the **State pays interest from its own funds** (the 15th FC later set **10 working days**).
[60:1:8] - **Attitude:** the Commission held that local bodies **need to be trusted and respected** as institutions of self-government, with minimal conditions.
[60:1:9] # Basic/performance grants and excluded areas – which FC
[60:1:10] - The **13th FC (2010-15)** first split local-body grants into a **general basic grant** and a **general performance grant**, and gave a **special area grant** to areas **outside Parts IX/IXA** (Fifth and **Sixth Schedule** areas).
[60:1:11] - The **14th FC gave no grant to Sixth Schedule / excluded areas** (Part IX does not apply; the Centre gave a one-time special assistance instead); the **15th FC** covered **all tiers** including **Fifth and Sixth Schedule areas and traditional bodies** – so the coverage **varies from Commission to Commission**.
[60:1:12] # Later Commissions
[60:1:13] TABLE head: FC (period) | Local-body grants | Split / conditions
  [60:1:13.0] 14th (2015-20) | ₹2,87,436 crore; Panchayats ₹2,00,292 crore | Basic:performance – GPs 90:10, municipalities 80:20
  [60:1:13.1] 15th (2021-26) | Rural ₹2.36 lakh crore | Tied : untied 60 : 40 (rural); tied for water and sanitation; audited accounts online and property-tax floor rates notified
  [60:1:13.2] 16th (2026-31) | ₹7,91,493 crore – rural ≈ ₹4.4 lakh crore, urban ≈ ₹3.6 lakh crore; urban share 45% (from 36%) | Basic and performance (80:20); only duly constituted bodies
[60:1:14] - **16th FC:** total grants **₹9.47 lakh crore**, only for **local bodies and disaster management**; **revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants dropped**.
[60:1:15] - **AP:** **₹28,785 crore** local-body grants (2026-31), of which **₹12,150 crore** is tied to holding local polls.
[60:1:16] > Asked as: 14th FC weights population:area (90:10 – 2 PYQs); basic:performance for GPs (90:10, not 80:20 – APPSC Group-II 2017); 15-day release with interest; grants direct to GPs; undisbursed performance grant; "trust and respect"; who introduced basic and performance grants (13th FC); Sixth Schedule areas.
[60:1:17] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity APPSC Part 18.1 (src/polity/nextgen-polity-appsc-26.txt) p.11-12; PMF Polity Part 3 (src/polity/pmf-polity-03.txt) p.39-40; 14th FC Report ch.9 and MoF guidelines of 8 Oct 2015 (fincomindia.nic.in); twd.tripura.gov.in Guidelines (excluded areas); app notes 2:60 sub 7
[60:1:18] - **AP's tax-devolution share** under the 16th FC rose to **4.217%** (from 4.05%) while revenue-deficit grants ended.
## SUB 2 | Union Finance Commission and Local Bodies – Article 280(3)(bb) and (c)
[60:2:0] - **Art. 280(3)(bb)** (Panchayats, 73rd) and **(c)** (Municipalities, 74th), added in **1992**: the Union FC recommends **measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State** to supplement the resources of local bodies **on the basis of the SFC's recommendations**.
[60:2:1] - So the Union FC **does have a role** in financial help to local bodies – "A: the Union FC has no role" and "R: it cannot recommend assistance to Panchayats" are **false**.
[60:2:2] - **Local government** remains a **State subject** – **Entry 5, State List** – despite the 73rd/74th Amendments (true).
[60:2:3] - Union FC grants to Panchayats rest on **Art. 280** and are **routed through the States**; **Art. 270** = divisible pool of Union taxes.
[60:2:4] > Asked as: assertion-reason (UPPCS 2011: A false, R true; UPPCS 2015: SFC constitutional – A true, R false).
[60:2:5] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch39 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.105; NextGen Polity APPSC Part 18.1 (src/polity/nextgen-polity-appsc-26.txt) p.10; app notes 2:60 sub 1
## SUB 3 | Panchayat Revenue – Own, Assigned and Shared (Andhra Pradesh)
[60:3:0] TABLE head: Source | Basis
  [60:3:0.0] Own taxes, duties, tolls, fees | Only if the State Legislature authorises (Art. 243H, "may")
  [60:3:0.1] Assigned taxes | State-levied/collected taxes handed over to Panchayats, on SFC advice
  [60:3:0.2] Shared taxes | Share of State taxes as per SFC
  [60:3:0.3] Grants-in-aid | State Consolidated Fund (243H / 243I)
  [60:3:0.4] Union FC grants | Art. 280, routed through the States
[60:3:1] - Panchayats have **no independent constitutional taxing power**.
[60:3:2] - **Property (house) tax** is a **local tax** and the **major own-source revenue** of Panchayats (APPSC GS 2018), as of ULBs.
[60:3:3] - **AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994:** a GP may levy a **surcharge on the seigniorage fee** collected by the Government on materials (other than minerals and minor minerals) **quarried in the village**; **seigniorage fees** go to the **Gram Panchayat Fund**.
[60:3:4] - **Transfer duty** – a **surcharge on stamp duty** on sale/transfer of immovable property in the GP area (**1.5%** in AP) – is collected by the State and credited to the GP **quarterly**.
[60:3:5] - **Land cess and registration (stamp-duty) surcharge** are **collected by the State Government and the share is transferred to the Gram Panchayat**.
[60:3:6] > Asked as: seigniorage surcharge (flashcard); surcharge on stamp duty on property transactions; land cess and registration surcharge; property tax a local tax.
[60:3:7] ~~ Sources: AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 s.60(4), s.69; Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch39 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.112 (taxes of Village Panchayats, cess on stamp duty); app notes 2:60 sub 3

  [60:4:2.6] Demographic performance | – | – | 12.5 | 10
  [60:4:2.7] Tax and fiscal effort | – | – | 2.5 | –
  [60:4:2.8] Contribution to GDP (new) | – | – | – | 10
[60:4:3] - **15th FC criteria other than population, area and income distance:** **demographic performance, forest and ecology, tax and fiscal effort** – **only three** (governance reforms and stable government were never criteria) – UPSC 2023.
[60:4:4] - **Income distance** always carries the **highest weight**.
[60:4:5] - **16th FC changes:** income distance from the **average of the three largest States**; demographic performance = **population growth 1971-2011** (15th: TFR); forest includes **open forests**; **contribution to GDP** replaced tax effort.
[60:4:6] - **AP:** "**prosperity paradox**" (above-average per capita GSDP hurts it under income distance); share **4.217%** (from 4.05%).
[60:4:7] - **Vertical devolution** = Union ↔ States; **horizontal** = among the States; **vertical fiscal imbalance** – the Union has the buoyant taxes, the States the heavier spending; **cesses and surcharges** are outside the divisible pool (≈ 81% of gross tax).
[60:4:8] > Asked as: how many of five listed items were 15th FC criteria (UPSC 2023 – only three).

## SUB 5 | Audit of Local Bodies
[60:5:0] - **Art. 243J / 243Z:** State law provides for the **maintenance and audit of accounts** of Panchayats/Municipalities.
[60:5:1] - **AP State Audit Act, 1989:** the **Local Fund Audit Department** was renamed the **State Audit Department**; the **Director of State Audit** (Finance Dept) is the **primary (statutory) auditor** of PRIs and can levy a **surcharge** for losses (s.10).
[60:5:2] - **CAG** gives only **Technical Guidance and Support (TGS)** over local-body audit – recommended by the **11th Finance Commission**.
[60:5:3] > Asked as: primary auditor of PRIs (Director, State Audit – not the CAG).

=== NOTES 2:61 | Challenges in Local Devolution – Funds, Functions, Functionaries; Parallel Bodies and Capacity Gaps
## SUB 0 | Devolution Index – Measuring Devolution to Panchayats
[61:0:0] # The report
[61:0:1] - **Devolution Index / Devolution Report** ("**Status of Devolution to Panchayats in States**"): **commissioned by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj (Central Government)** to assess the States' **policy and legislative framework and its outcomes** for Panchayati Raj – not a "PR Dashboard" or a progress report.
[61:0:2] - It measures the **actual devolution of functions, funds and functionaries** (devolution **in policy and in practice**), not merely expected devolution or funds alone.
[61:0:3] - **Who prepared it:** **IIPA** (earlier editions and the **2024** edition), but the **2014-15 and 2015-16 reports were entrusted to the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS)**, Mumbai – not NIRD or NCAER.
[61:0:4] # TISS 2015-16 index design (score out of 100)
[61:0:5] TABLE head: Dimension | Weight | Components
  [61:0:5.0] Operational core of decentralisation | 90% | Functions 10, Functionaries 15, Finances 50, Autonomy 15
  [61:0:5.1] Support systems for devolution / decentralisation | 10% | Capacity building 2, constitutional mechanisms (SFC, DPC) 5, accountability and transparency 3
[61:0:6] # Awards
[61:0:7] - **Incremental Devolution Index award 2015-16:** **Andhra Pradesh, Sikkim and Odisha** were the top performers (short-term progress 2012-15) – so "**all of the given options**".
[61:0:8] - Presented by the **Prime Minister** on **National Panchayati Raj Day, 24 April 2016** (Jamshedpur) – AP's award in **April 2016** was the **Incremental Devolution Index Award**, not a Best/Swachh/ODF award.
[61:0:9] # 2024 Index (released Feb 2025, MoPR with IIPA, 6 dimensions)
[61:0:10] - **Six dimensions:** Framework, Functions, Finances, Functionaries, **Capacity Enhancement**, **Accountability**.
[61:0:11] TABLE head: 2024 Index | Top / score
  [61:0:11.0] Overall | Karnataka 1st, then Kerala, Tamil Nadu
  [61:0:11.1] Functions / Finances / Functionaries | Tamil Nadu / Karnataka / Gujarat
  [61:0:11.2] AP | 54.43, medium band (Telangana 55.1)
[61:0:12] > Asked as: what the index measures; which report the Centre commissions; who prepared 2015-16 (TISS); weight of support systems (10%); Incremental Devolution Index award to AP (April 2016, 2 PYQs).
[61:0:13] ~~ Sources: TISS, Devolution Report 2015-16 for MoPR, p.7 and Fig. 2.1 p.54 (cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in); OdishaTV and Hans India, 25 Apr 2016; app notes 2:61 sub 0
## SUB 1 | Capacity Building and Accountability Institutions
[61:1:0] TABLE head: Body / tool | Feature
  [61:1:0.0] NIRDPR | National Institute of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj – national training body, Hyderabad
  [61:1:0.1] APSIRD & PR | AP State Institute of Rural Development and Panchayat Raj – the State capacity-building institute
  [61:1:0.2] eGramSwaraj | Planning, accounting, reporting; launched with SVAMITVA 24 April 2020
  [61:1:0.3] AuditOnline | Online audit of Panchayat accounts
  [61:1:0.4] SVAMITVA | Drone survey by the Survey of India; "Record of Rights", property-tax baseline
[61:1:1] - **Ombudsman for local bodies in AP:** the function is entrusted to the **Lokayukta** (not the CAG or a banking/insurance ombudsman).
[61:1:2] - **Second ARC, 6th Report "Local Governance" (2007):** recommended a **Local Body Ombudsman**; **Kerala:** **Ombudsman for Local Self Government Institutions** (2001 amendment of the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act).
[61:1:3] - **V. Ramachandran Expert Committee (MoPR, 2013):** Panchayats for **delivery of public services**.
[61:1:4] # RGSA
[61:1:5] - **RGSA** (**2018-19**) strengthens PRIs for the **SDGs**; **117 aspirational districts**; converges with **Mission Antyodaya**.
[61:1:6] - **Revamped RGSA: 1 April 2022 – 31 March 2026** (co-terminus with the 15th FC) – not 1 April 2021.
[61:1:7] - Funding **60:40**; NE and hilly States **90:10**; **UTs 100%** Central.
[61:1:8] - **BRGF merged into RGSA** (APPSC GS 2018).
[61:1:9] > Asked as: NIRD location (Hyderabad); AP's State institute (APSIRD & PR); local-body ombudsman in AP (Lokayukta).
[61:1:10] ~~ Sources: nirdpr.org.in; AP Lokayukta Act, 1983 (as amended for local bodies); app notes 2:61 sub 6-7
## SUB 2 | The 3Fs – Functions, Funds, Functionaries
[61:2:0] TABLE head: F | Meaning | Reality
  [61:2:0.0] Functions | Eleventh Schedule 29 (Panchayats), Twelfth Schedule 18 (Municipalities) | Devolved on paper
  [61:2:0.1] Funds | Untied money matching functions | Tied to schemes
  [61:2:0.2] Functionaries | Staff answerable to the local body | Report to State line departments
[61:2:1] - **Arts 243G / 243W say "may"** – the Schedules transfer nothing automatically; devolution is discretionary.
[61:2:2] - **Roadmap for Panchayati Raj / Laxmikanth:** weak 3Fs, **excessive bureaucratic control**, **tied funds**, **dependence on grants**, **reluctance to tax**, parallel bodies → PRIs are **implementing agencies, not planning units**.
[61:2:3] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch39 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.112-113; app notes 2:61 sub 0
## SUB 3 | Funds Gap and the 16th FC Conditions
[61:3:0] - **Property tax** = main ULB own revenue, **under-assessed and under-collected**.
[61:3:1] - ULB own revenue ≈ **0.3% of GDP**; cities ≈ **2/3 of GDP**.
[61:3:2] - **16th FC:** urban share **36% → 45%**; grants **80% basic, 20% performance**.
[61:3:3] - **Conditions:** **properly constituted local bodies**, **published audited accounts**, **timely SFCs** – so delayed polls put grants at risk; **SFC reports are often ignored** by States.
[61:3:4] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch39 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.112; PMF Polity Part 3 (src/polity/pmf-polity-03.txt) p.40; app notes 2:61 sub 2
## SUB 4 | Parallel Bodies and Bureaucratic Control
[61:4:0] TABLE head: Body / control | Effect
  [61:4:0.0] DRDAs, user groups, SHGs, MPLADS / MLA LADS | Run schemes outside PRIs; legislators pick works
  [61:4:0.1] Janmabhoomi committees (2014-19); village/ward secretariats and volunteers (2019) – AP | Parallel to GPs and wards
  [61:4:0.2] Special Officers (AP) | Run lapsed local bodies
[61:4:1] - **MPLADS:** MP recommends → **Implementing District Authority** executes; RTI applies; **eSAKSHI** portal.
[61:4:2] - **Balwantrai Mehta Committee:** the **Collector chairs the Zilla Parishad**.
[61:4:3] - DPC (243ZD) and MPC (243ZE) are **constitutional** planning bodies, not parallel bodies.
[61:4:4] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch39 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.113; app notes 2:61 sub 3
## SUB 5 | Key Articles on Local Bodies
[61:5:0] TABLE head: Article | Provision
  [61:5:0.0] 243K / 243ZA | SEC appointed by the Governor; removed like a High Court judge (CEC like a Supreme Court judge)
  [61:5:0.1] 243E / 243U | 5-year term; polls before expiry or within 6 months of dissolution
  [61:5:0.2] 243D | Women at least one-third; AP gives 50%
  [61:5:0.3] 243ZD / 243ZE | DPC / MPC – integration of district / metropolitan plans
[61:5:1] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch39-40 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.104-106; app notes 2:61 sub 1
## SUB 6 | Women Representatives – the Proxy Problem
[61:6:0] - **"Sarpanch pati":** a male relative rules in her name; proxy behaviour **falls markedly in her second term**.
[61:6:1] - **MoPR advisory committee (Sushil Kumar, 2025):** **exemplary penalties** in proven proxy cases.
[61:6:2] - **Sashakt Panchayat-Netri Abhiyan** and **Model Women-Friendly GPs:** strengthen the **participation and leadership of elected women representatives**.
[61:6:3] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:61 sub 5
## SUB 7 | Andhra Pradesh Local Body Elections (2026)
[61:7:0] - AP Mandal and Zilla Parishad polls due by **23 Sep 2026**; **₹12,150 crore** of 16th FC grants at risk if polls are delayed.
[61:7:1] - **AP Cabinet (18 Aug 2026):** BC reservation **34% rural, 33⅓% urban**; **direct election of Mayors and chairpersons**.
[61:7:2] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:61 sub 4 (as of 2026)

=== NOTES 2:62 | Election Commission of India – Composition, Appointment (2023 Act), Powers and Functions
## SUB 0 | Chief Election Commissioners – Firsts, Tenures and Personalities

## SUB 1 | Appointment, Tenure, Removal and Status of the CEC and ECs
[62:1:0] # Appointment
[62:1:1] - **Art. 324(2):** the CEC and other ECs are appointed by the **President** (subject to any law of Parliament) – **not** elected by Parliament, not appointed by the PM, the Home Minister or the CJI.
[62:1:2] - **Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India (2 March 2023, Constitution Bench):** until Parliament made a law, appointment on the advice of **PM + Leader of Opposition (or leader of the largest opposition party) in Lok Sabha + CJI**; it also said it is **desirable** that **other ECs** be removable only on the grounds of an SC judge – it said nothing about **Regional Commissioners**.
[62:1:3] - **CEC and Other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023** (Act 49 of 2023; replaced the **1991 Act**):
[62:1:4] TABLE head: Stage | Composition / rule
  [62:1:4.0] Search Committee | Headed by the Law Minister + two Secretary-rank members; shortlists five names
  [62:1:4.1] Selection Committee | PM (chair), LoP / largest opposition party leader in Lok Sabha, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM (replaces the CJI); may pick names outside the shortlist
  [62:1:4.2] Appointment | President, on the Selection Committee's recommendation
[62:1:5] - Criticism: gives the government a **2:1** majority; challenged by ADR and **Jaya Thakur (Jaya Thakur v. Union of India)** – pending as of 2026.
[62:1:6] # Committees that recommended a three-member ECI
[62:1:7] - **Dinesh Goswami Committee on Electoral Reforms (1990)** – appointed by the V.P. Singh Government, chaired by Law Minister Dinesh Goswami; first main recommendation: **"Election Commission to be a three-member body"**, CEC appointed in consultation with the **CJI and LoP**.
[62:1:8] - **Tarkunde Committee (1974-75)** – **unofficial**, set up by **Jayaprakash Narayan**; also proposed a multi-member Commission chosen by a PM-LoP-CJI panel. **Rajamannar** and **Sarkaria** dealt with Centre-State relations.
[62:1:9] # Tenure, salary and status
[62:1:10] TABLE head: Item | Rule
  [62:1:10.0] Term | 6 years or age 65, whichever is earlier (1991 Act; 2023 Act s.9 – no reappointment); may resign by writing to the President
  [62:1:10.1] Powers and pay | CEC and ECs have equal powers and equal salary = a Judge of the Supreme Court; differences decided by majority
  [62:1:10.2] Status | The CEC's status is that of a Supreme Court judge (pay, removal) – not that of a Governor or a Speaker
  [62:1:10.3] Service conditions | Cannot be varied to the CEC's disadvantage after appointment (Art. 324(5))
[62:1:11] - **Not** "5 years or 62" and **not** "equal powers but unequal salaries" (both wrong – UPSC 2002).
[62:1:12] # Removal (Art. 324(5))
[62:1:13] TABLE head: Office | How removed
  [62:1:13.0] CEC | Only in like manner and on like grounds as a Supreme Court judge – by the President on an address of both Houses passed by special majority on proved misbehaviour or incapacity; motion needs 100 Lok Sabha / 50 Rajya Sabha signatures (Judges Inquiry Act)
  [62:1:13.1] Election Commissioners and Regional Commissioners | By the President on the recommendation of the CEC – so the CEC's security of tenure is not available to them
  [62:1:13.2] State Election Commissioner | Like a High Court judge (Art. 243K(2))
[62:1:14] # Gaps the Constitution leaves
[62:1:15] - **No qualifications** and **no term** prescribed for members; **retiring ECs are not debarred** from further government appointment (contrast **CAG – Art. 148(4)**, **UPSC Chairman – Art. 319**). (NextGen's "ineligible for office of profit after retirement" is **not** a constitutional bar.)
[62:1:16] - ECI expenses are **not charged** on the Consolidated Fund (a long-standing demand); it depends on the Law, Home and DoPT Ministries.
[62:1:17] > Asked as: who appoints (5 PYQs); how the CEC / an EC is removed (5 PYQs); term 6 years or 65 (statements); equal powers and SC-judge salary; status of the CEC; committee that recommended three members (Goswami); post-retirement bar (APPSC G1 2024 – false).

## SUB 2 | Constitutional Status and Composition – Single-Member to Multi-Member
[62:2:0] # Status
[62:2:1] - A **permanent, independent constitutional body** set up directly by the Constitution – **Part XV ("Elections"), Articles 324-329**; basis **Art. 324**; an **all-India body common to the Centre and the States**.
[62:2:2] - Art. 324 is a **"reservoir of power"** (Mohinder Singh Gill, 1978) – used only where **no law holds the field**.
[62:2:3] - Seat **Nirvachan Sadan**, New Delhi; training arm **IIIDEM**, New Delhi.
[62:2:4] # Composition (Art. 324(2)-(4))
[62:2:5] - **CEC + such number of ECs as the President fixes**; today **CEC + 2 ECs = a three-member body** (APPSC G2 2025 – "three member body" and "constitutional body" are true; "appointed by the CJI" is false).
[62:2:6] - The CEC acts as **chairman**; the President may appoint **Regional Commissioners** after **consulting the Election Commission**.
[62:2:7] - All members have **equal powers**; decisions by **majority** – upheld in **T.N. Seshan v. Union of India (1995)**.
[62:2:8] # Single-member to multi-member
[62:2:9] TABLE head: Period | Status
  [62:2:9.0] 1950 – 15 Oct 1989 | Single-member – CEC only (originally one)
  [62:2:9.1] 16 Oct 1989 | Two ECs added – first three-member Commission (work grew after the 61st Amendment cut the voting age 21 → 18)
  [62:2:9.2] Jan 1990 | Posts abolished – single-member again
  [62:2:9.3] 1 Oct 1993 onwards | Multi-member (CEC + 2 ECs) continuously
[62:2:10] - So the ECI was **not** multi-member "since inception"; "made multi-member / three-member" in a 1987-1990 option set = **1989**.
[62:2:11] > Asked as: three-member year (1989 – 5 PYQs); originally how many (one); present strength (three); statements on status and composition; equal powers (an "except" item).
[62:2:12] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity APPSC Part 25 (src/polity/nextgen-polity-appsc-25.txt) p.15; Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch43 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.598-599; NCERT Polity summary (src/polity/onlyias-ncert-polity-02.txt) p.50; Rocket Polity (src/polity/rocket-polity-01.txt) p.62; app notes 2:62 sub 0-1
## SUB 3 | Powers and Functions of the ECI
[62:3:0] # Three kinds – administrative, advisory, quasi-judicial
[62:3:1] - Superintendence, direction and control of **electoral rolls** and **conduct of elections** to **Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President** (Art. 324(1)); decides **every aspect from the announcement of elections to the declaration of results** (APPSC G1 2023).
[62:3:2] - **Officers on election duty work under the ECI's control**, not the government's; staff preparing rolls are deemed on **deputation** to the ECI. It can issue guidelines and order **transfers/suspension** – it does **not** order the government to **dismiss** officials.
[62:3:3] - Delimits constituencies on the basis of the **Delimitation Commission Acts**; prepares and revises **electoral rolls** – **Special Intensive Revision** under **Art. 324 + Section 21, RPA 1950**.
[62:3:4] - Notifies **dates and schedules** (the Home Ministry has no such role), scrutinises nominations, fixes **expenditure limits**, can **cancel polls** for booth capturing or rigging.
[62:3:5] - **Recognises parties and allots symbols** (**Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968**) and acts as a court on **splits/mergers and symbol disputes** – not the Speaker, PM or President.
[62:3:6] - **Model Code of Conduct** – not a statute; rests on **Art. 324**; applies **from the announcement of the schedule** (**Harbans Singh Jalal, 1997**); **Part VII** = party in power.
[62:3:7] - Advises the **President on MPs' disqualification (Art. 103)** – the **President decides after obtaining the ECI's opinion and acts on it** – and the **Governor on MLAs' (Art. 192)**.
[62:3:8] - Advises the President whether elections can be held in a State under **President's Rule** (for extension beyond one year) – it does **not recommend** President's Rule.
[62:3:9] # What it does NOT do
[62:3:10] - **Election disputes:** decided by **courts** – election petitions under **RPA 1951** go to the **High Court** (appeal to SC); President/VP disputes to the **Supreme Court (Art. 71)**. The ECI **cannot** give the final verdict on disputes and does not try petitions.
[62:3:11] - **Anti-defection (Tenth Schedule)** → **Speaker/Chairman**.
[62:3:12] - Delimitation of J&K (2022) was by a Commission under **Justice Ranjana Desai**; **Assam** was delimited by the **ECI itself** (effective Aug 2023).
[62:3:13] > Asked as: functions statements (UPSC 1994, 2004, UPUDA 2001, APPSC G1 2023); symbol allotment; disqualification of an MP (President on ECI advice – 2 PYQs); Article 324 (2 PYQs); what the ECI cannot do (disputes, President's Rule).
[62:3:14] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity APPSC Part 26 (src/polity/nextgen-polity-appsc-26.txt) p.2-3; Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch43 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.601-602; Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch83 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.826; Rocket Polity (src/polity/rocket-polity-01.txt) p.63-64; NCERT Class IX Democratic Politics Ch.3 "Independent Election Commission" (src/polity/onlyias-ncert-polity-02.txt) p.50; app notes 2:62 sub 5, 8
## SUB 4 | Elections Conducted by the ECI and by the State Election Commission
[62:4:0] TABLE head: Under the ECI (Art. 324) | Not under the ECI
  [62:4:0.0] Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha | Panchayats and Municipalities → State Election Commission (Arts. 243K – panchayats, 243ZA – municipalities)
  [62:4:0.1] State Assemblies and Councils | Speaker, Deputy Speaker – chosen by the House (Art. 93; States Art. 178)
  [62:4:0.2] President and Vice-President | Deputy Chairman, RS (Art. 89(2)); Chairman of a Legislative Council (Art. 182)
[62:4:1] - So "the ECI administers elections to Panchayats and Municipalities" is **false**; co-operative societies and banks are not SEC elections either.
[62:4:2] TABLE head: Basis | ECI | SEC | Chief Electoral Officer
  [62:4:2.0] Source | Art. 324, Part XV | Arts. 243K, 243ZA (73rd/74th Amendments, 1992) | Sec. 13A, RPA 1950 – not a constitutional authority
  [62:4:2.1] Appointed by | President | Governor | ECI, in consultation with the State Government
  [62:4:2.2] Removal | Like an SC judge | Like a High Court judge (243K(2)) | By the ECI
[62:4:3] - **District:** the **Collector = District Election Officer / District Returning Officer**; appoints **Returning and Presiding Officers**.
[62:4:4] - **AP:** State Election Commissioner **Anil Chandra Punetha** (local-body polls).
[62:4:5] - Other facts for app MCQs: emergency provisions are **Part XVIII**; the federal-to-unitary switch in an Emergency is a **unique feature** of the Constitution (Laxmikanth), **not** borrowed from Weimar (Weimar = suspension of FRs).
[62:4:6] > Asked as: who conducts State Assembly / Presidential polls (ECI); who conducts local-body polls (SEC – 4 PYQs); which election is not by the ECI (local bodies); SEC removal like an HC judge; statements mixing ECI and Part XVIII.
[62:4:7] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch43 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.598; Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch3 Salient Features (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-01.txt) pdf p.69; Rocket Polity (src/polity/rocket-polity-01.txt) p.62-63, p.91; NextGen Polity APPSC Part 25 (src/polity/nextgen-polity-appsc-25.txt) p.1-3; app notes 2:62 sub 6-7
[62:4:8] - **Panchayats** = **entry 5 of the State List**; the State Government decides when panchayat polls are held, the SEC conducts them.

## SUB 6 | Voter Facilitation – SVEEP, Apps, Home Voting and VVPAT
[62:6:0] TABLE head: App / campaign | Purpose
  [62:6:0.0] SVEEP | Systematic Voters' Education and Electoral Participation – voter awareness
  [62:6:0.1] cVIGIL | Citizens report MCC and expenditure violations with time-stamped evidence; status within 100 minutes
  [62:6:0.2] Saksham-ECI | Registration and polling-station help for persons with disabilities (in news March 2024); developed with the Department of Empowerment of PwDs
  [62:6:0.3] Voter Helpline | Search name, forms, complaints; toll-free 1950
[62:6:1] - **ECI + Indian Railways (March 2019):** four long-distance trains carried **voter-awareness** messages (SVEEP) for the Lok Sabha polls; Railways got the ECI's Best Electoral Practices Award 2024-25.
[62:6:2] - **Home voting:** voters **above 85** and PwDs with **40% benchmark disability**.
[62:6:3] - **VVPAT:** **8 April 2019** – SC raised verification to **five** EVMs-VVPATs per Assembly segment; **ADR v. ECI (26 April 2024)** – **100% VVPAT count rejected**; symbol loading units sealed **45 days**; verification request within **7 days** at the candidate's cost.
[62:6:4] > Asked as: ECI app for PwDs (Saksham); agency the ECI partnered for voter awareness (Indian Railways).
[62:6:5] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:62 sub 5; PIB / Business Standard "EC, Railways join hands to create voter awareness" (29-03-2019); ECI press notes on Saksham-ECI
## SUB 7 | Election Disputes and Polling-Day Situations
[62:7:0] - **Art. 329(a):** laws on delimitation and allotment of seats **cannot be questioned in court**.
[62:7:1] - **Art. 329(b):** an election to Parliament/State Legislature can be challenged **only by an election petition** under **RPA 1951** – tried by the **High Court** (original jurisdiction), appeal to the **Supreme Court**.
[62:7:2] - **Art. 71:** President/VP election disputes → **Supreme Court**. The ECI **cannot review a declared result**.
[62:7:3] TABLE head: RPA 1951 section | Situation | Action
  [62:7:3.0] 57 | Riot, open violence, natural calamity | Presiding or Returning Officer adjourns; resumes with ECI approval; only those who had not voted may vote
  [62:7:3.1] 58 | EVM/ballot box unlawfully taken, destroyed or tampered | ECI declares the poll void, fixes a fresh poll
  [62:7:3.2] 58A | Booth capturing | Adjournment or countermand
[62:7:4] > Asked as: kept for the app MCQs (the one PYQ on election-petition jurisdiction is filed under row 63).

=== NOTES 2:63 | Elections – Delimitation, Model Code of Conduct, Evm-vvpat, Nota, Election Petitions
## SUB 0 | Part XV and the Right to Vote – Articles 324-329, Adult Suffrage
[63:0:0] # Part XV – Elections (Articles 324-329)
[63:0:1] TABLE head: Article | Content
  [63:0:1.0] 324 | Election Commission: superintendence, direction and control of electoral rolls and of all elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President; 324(2): CEC + other ECs as the President fixes
  [63:0:1.1] 325 | One general electoral roll for every territorial constituency; no one excluded on grounds only of religion, race, caste or sex
  [63:0:1.2] 326 | Elections to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies on the basis of adult suffrage (universal franchise)
  [63:0:1.3] 327 / 328 | Parliament / State Legislature may make laws on elections
  [63:0:1.4] 329 | Bar on courts: delimitation laws cannot be questioned; an election can be challenged only by an election petition
[63:0:2] - Elections are in **Part XV** (not XIV, XVI or XVII). Correct pair: **ECI – Art. 324** (Supreme Court = 124, UPSC = 315, Attorney General = 76); Art. 280 = Finance Commission; **Art. 171** = Legislative Councils, not elections.
[63:0:3] - ECI set up on **25 January 1950** – permanent constitutional body; its institute **IIIDEM** trains election managers. **Mohinder Singh Gill v CEC (1978)**: Art. 324 is a "**reservoir of power**" where Parliament has not legislated.
[63:0:4] - **ECI** conducts Lok Sabha, Assembly, Rajya Sabha, Council, **President and Vice-President** polls and prepares **electoral rolls / registers voters**; **State Election Commissions** (Arts. **243K, 243ZA**) run panchayat and municipal polls.
[63:0:5] - Qualifications/disqualifications: **Art. 84 / 102** (Parliament), **173 / 191** (State Legislatures). Simultaneous polls would need amending **Arts. 83** (duration of Houses), **85, 172, 174, 356**.
[63:0:6] # Adult suffrage
[63:0:7] - **Art. 326**: every citizen aged **18+** may vote unless disqualified by law for **non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime, corrupt or illegal practice** – universal franchise "subject to limitations by statute".
[63:0:8] - Voting age **21 → 18**: **61st Amendment Act, 1988** (in force **28 March 1989**); 18-year-olds first voted in the **1989** Lok Sabha election (not 59th, 60th, 63rd, 69th or 73rd).
[63:0:9] - Principles for Lok Sabha/Assembly elections (UPPSC 2011): adult suffrage, **one roll per territorial constituency**, no exclusion on religion, race, sex (Arts. 325-326); the UPPSC key also accepted "parties free to have their own norms" (All four).
[63:0:10] - Democracy needs **political parties, an electorate, an independent judiciary and universal adult suffrage** (UPSC 1994: all four).
[63:0:11] - Right to vote and to contest = **statutory rights** (**Kuldip Nayar v UoI, 2006**), not Fundamental Rights; with the right to petition they are **political rights** – the **right to life** (Art. 21) is a civil right.
[63:0:12] - **Who cannot vote:** a person **confined in prison** (Sec. 62(5) RPA 1951); **preventive detenus** vote by **postal ballot**. **Overseas electors** (Sec. **20A** RPA 1950, 2010): Indian **citizen**, enrolled at the **passport address**, must vote **in person** in India.
[63:0:13] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 02 p.2-3, 20 p.7-8; NextGen Rocket Polity 01 p.63-64; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.81-83
## SUB 1 | General Elections – Dates, Firsts and Records
[63:1:0] # Lok Sabha general elections
[63:1:1] TABLE head: Lok Sabha | Election
  [63:1:1.0] 1st | 25 Oct 1951 – 21 Feb 1952 ("1951-52"; 489 seats; first session 13 May 1952) – the longest poll (about 4 months)
  [63:1:1.1] 5th | 1971 – the first mid-term election (4th Lok Sabha dissolved early)
  [63:1:1.2] 8th | 1984 – turnout about 64%, the record until 2014; last single-party (Congress) majority till 2014
  [63:1:1.3] 9th | 1989 – first poll with 18-year-old voters; end of the "Congress system" (coalition era)
  [63:1:1.4] 12th | Feb-March 1998 (constituted 10 March 1998)
  [63:1:1.5] 15th | 16 April – 13 May 2009; about 714 million electors
  [63:1:1.6] 16th | 7 April – 12 May 2014; turnout 66.4%; first Lok Sabha poll with NOTA
  [63:1:1.7] 17th | 11 April – 19 May 2019; 7 phases; record turnout 67.4%
  [63:1:1.8] 18th | 19 April – 1 June 2024 (44 days – 2nd longest after 1951-52)
[63:1:2] - **18 general elections** so far (2024 = 18th); a 2019 question's "17" was right then.
[63:1:3] - **Congress** won a Lok Sabha majority alone in 1952-1971, 1980 and **1984 (8th, the last)**; it lost in 1977 and 1989.
[63:1:4] - **Longest poll:** 1951-52 (then 2024, 44 days). 1999 (5 Sept – 3 Oct) was only the longest of 1999/2004/2009 – the 1951-52 poll was longer, so "None" is the answer.
[63:1:5] - **Shyam Saran Negi** (Kalpa, Kinnaur, HP): independent India's **first voter** (Oct 1951), voted in **every general election** till 2022; honoured by CEC **Navin Chawla** (2010).
[63:1:6] - **Atal Bihari Vajpayee**: only MP elected from **four States** (UP, MP, Delhi, Gujarat). **Narendra Modi**: **Varanasi** (2014, 2019, 2024).
[63:1:7] - 543 elected Lok Sabha seats in 2009: **530 from States**, 13 from UTs.
[63:1:8] # By-polls and State polls asked
[63:1:9] - **Srinagar Lok Sabha by-poll (April 2017)**: turnout only **7.14%** amid violence.
[63:1:10] - **AP by-elections** to 18 Assembly seats + Nellore Lok Sabha: **12 June 2012**. **UP Assembly 2017**: **7 phases**.

## SUB 2 | Reservation of Seats – Articles 330-334 and Anglo-Indians
[63:2:0] TABLE head: Article | Provision
  [63:2:0.0] 330 | Seats reserved for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha, in proportion to their population
  [63:2:0.1] 331 | President nominated 2 Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha
  [63:2:0.2] 332 | SC/ST seats in State Assemblies
  [63:2:0.3] 333 | Governor nominated 1 Anglo-Indian to the Assembly
  [63:2:0.4] 334 | Time limit: originally 10 years (till 1960), extended by successive amendments (79th, 1999 → 2010; 95th, 2009 → 2020); 104th (2019) → SC/ST till 2030, Anglo-Indian nomination ended from 25 Jan 2020
  [63:2:0.5] 334A | Women one-third – 106th Amendment (2023), for 15 years; starts after the next census and delimitation
[63:2:1] - Anglo-Indian nomination **ceased in 2020** (not 2030, 2035, 2040); "Only A" (President 2, Governor 1) was correct before 2020.
[63:2:2] - Reserved seats have a **common electorate** – all voters of the constituency vote; ST seats go where the ST share is highest, SC seats are spread and rotated.
[63:2:3] - SC seats in a State follow its SC population share: **undivided AP (42 Lok Sabha seats) had 7 SC and 3 ST** after 2008 (6 SC before).
[63:2:4] - **Madhya Pradesh** has the most ST-reserved Lok Sabha seats (**6**).
[63:2:5] - **Municipalities (Art. 243T)**: not less than **one-third** of SC/ST seats reserved for SC/ST **women**.
[63:2:6] TABLE head: State | Lok Sabha SC / ST | Assembly SC / ST
  [63:2:6.0] Andhra Pradesh (25 LS, 175 MLA) | 4 SC (Amalapuram, Bapatla, Chittoor, Tirupati) / 1 ST (Araku) – Nellore is general | 29 / 7 (AP Reorganisation Act, 2014)
  [63:2:6.1] Telangana (17 LS, 119 MLA) | 3 SC (Peddapalle, Warangal, Nagarkurnool) / 2 ST (Adilabad, Mahabubabad) | 19 / 12
