=== NOTES 2:70 | Finance Commission – Composition, Terms of Reference, Functions; 15TH and 16TH Finance Commission
## SUB 0 | Finance Commission – Article 280, Composition and Qualifications
[70:0:0] # Constitutional basis
[70:0:1] - **Article 280** (Part **XII**) provides for the Finance Commission (FC), a **quasi-judicial constitutional body**; Articles **280 and 281** deal with it (Art. **290** = pensions, not the FC; Art. 148 = CAG).
[70:0:2] - Constituted by the **President** within two years of the Constitution's start and then **every fifth year or earlier** as he considers necessary – a **temporary** body, not permanent.
[70:0:3] - The Constitution envisages the FC as the **balancing wheel of fiscal federalism** (Laxmikanth); "Federal Finance Commission" = finances **between the Centre and the States**.
[70:0:4] - **Art. 281:** the **President** lays every recommendation, with an **explanatory memorandum** on the action taken, before each House of Parliament.
[70:0:5] - Recommendations are **advisory, not binding**; **P.V. Rajamannar** (4th FC): they should not be turned down without **very compelling reasons**.
[70:0:6] # Composition and qualifications
[70:0:7] - **Chairman + four other members** (5 in all), appointed by the **President** (Art. 280(1)) – not a Chairman and six members.
[70:0:8] - They hold office for **such period as the President specifies**; members are **eligible for reappointment**; no term fixed in the Constitution.
[70:0:9] - **Parliament** fixes qualifications and manner of selection (Art. 280(2)) – the **Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951** (not the President, the Union Cabinet or the Finance Minister).
[70:0:10] TABLE head: Post | Qualification (1951 Act)
  [70:0:10.0] Chairman | Experience in public affairs
  [70:0:10.1] Member | High Court judge or qualified to be one (one of the possible fields – not compulsory)
  [70:0:10.2] Member | Special knowledge of government finance and accounts
  [70:0:10.3] Member | Wide experience in financial matters and administration
  [70:0:10.4] Member | Special knowledge of economics
[70:0:11] - There is no member post for a monetary policy expert or a Parliament member.
[70:0:12] - The FC has the **powers of a civil court** (summoning persons, production of documents).
[70:0:13] - It reports to the **President**, not to NITI Aayog or Parliament directly.
[70:0:14] - The **101st Amendment (2016)** introduced **GST** – it did not implement any FC report.
[70:0:15] > Statement items test: Art. 280 vs 290, "every fifth year", Chairman + 4, Parliament (not President) fixes qualifications, report → President → Art. 281.
[70:0:16] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 20 p.6-7, 26 p.10-12; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.46 p.614-616
[70:0:17] - **First FC Chairman: K.C. Neogy** (not K. Santhanam, who chaired the 2nd).
## SUB 1 | Functions – Article 280(3) and the Divisible Pool
[70:1:0] # Functions (Art. 280(3)) – recommendations to the President
[70:1:1] - 1. **Distribution of the net proceeds of taxes** between the Centre and the States (**vertical**) and **allocation among the States** (**horizontal**).
[70:1:2] - 2. **Principles governing grants-in-aid** to the States out of the **Consolidated Fund of India** (Art. **275**).
[70:1:3] - 3. **Measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State** to supplement the resources of **Panchayats and Municipalities**, on the basis of the **State Finance Commission**'s recommendations (added by the **73rd/74th Amendments, 1992**).
[70:1:4] - 4. **Any other matter** referred by the President **in the interests of sound finance**.
[70:1:5] - Till 1960 it also suggested grants to Assam, Bihar, Odisha and West Bengal in lieu of jute export duty (Art. 273).
[70:1:6] - **Main function:** deciding the **share of States in Central taxes** – the body that recommends the principles of sharing revenues (not the Inter-State Council, NDC, NITI Aayog, Planning Commission or Finance Ministry).
[70:1:7] - **Not FC functions:** allocation of funds to constitutional bodies, maintaining income-expenditure details of governments, financial control over the Centre or States, fixing **GST rates**, releasing funds.
[70:1:8] - **Agricultural income tax** is a **State** tax (State List entry 46) – the Constitution assigns it; UPSC 1995's key names the FC as the body linked to sharing taxes with States.
[70:1:9] # Divisible pool
[70:1:10] - **Divisible pool** = gross tax revenue − **cesses, surcharges** and **cost of collection**; the **CAG certifies** net proceeds (Art. 279).
[70:1:11] - Rising **cesses and surcharges** shrink the divisible pool, so the States' real share of gross tax revenue is below the headline %.
[70:1:12] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 20 p.7, 26 p.10, 12; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.46 p.614-615

  [70:2:0.0] 1st | K.C. Neogy (set up 1951 by Presidential order; 6 April 1952) | 1952–57 | –
  [70:2:0.1] 2nd | K. Santhanam | 1957–62 | –

[70:2:3] - **M.V. Mathur** (member, 3rd FC, 1960) suggested **merging the Finance and Planning Commissions**.
[70:2:4] - 15th FC award "2020-25" is a trap: first report 2020-21 (Dec 2019) + main report 2021-26 (Nov 2020).
[70:2:5] > Chairman matches recur: 10th Pant – 11th Khusro – 12th Rangarajan – 13th Kelkar – 14th Reddy – 15th Singh – 16th Panagariya.
[70:2:6] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.46 Table 46.1 p.615-616; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 26 p.10; app's current notes (row 70)
## SUB 3 | 14th Finance Commission (2015–20)
[70:3:0] - Constituted **2 January 2013** (Y.V. Reddy); award **1 April 2015 – 31 March 2020**; GoI accepted the report on **24 February 2015**.
[70:3:1] - Share in the divisible pool raised **32% → 42%** – the **largest increase ever**.
[70:3:2] - **Tax devolution = the primary route** of transfer (a "compositional shift" from grants to devolution); **sector-specific grants dropped**; ignored the **Plan/non-Plan** distinction.
[70:3:3] - Made **no distinction** between **special and general category** States – a formula-based mechanism with no room for political bargaining (the Constitution has no provision for Special Category Status).
[70:3:4] - **Base year** for its projections: **2014-15** (reassessed base year).
[70:3:5] - Population base: **1971 and 2011**; **fiscal discipline** dropped as a criterion; **forest cover** added.
[70:3:6] TABLE head: Criterion (14th FC) | Weight
  [70:3:6.0] Income distance | 50% (highest)
  [70:3:6.1] Population 1971 | 17.5%
  [70:3:6.2] Population 2011 (demographic change) | 10%
  [70:3:6.3] Area | 15%
  [70:3:6.4] Forest cover | 7.5%
[70:3:7] - **Andhra Pradesh's share: 4.305%** (residuary AP, first award after bifurcation).
[70:3:8] - Local-body grants **₹2,87,436 crore** (panchayats ₹2,00,292 crore) as **basic and performance** grants to duly constituted bodies (2011 population 90%, area 10%).
[70:3:9] - After the 42% award the Centre raised **non-shareable cesses**.
[70:3:10] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 26 p.11-12; NextGen Indian Economy P1 - APPSC 01; 14th FC report (fincomindia.nic.in) vol. I ch. Re-assessment of the base year
## SUB 4 | Grants, Disaster Funds, Special Category Status and Andhra Pradesh
[70:4:0] # Grants and disaster funds
[70:4:1] TABLE head: FC | Notable recommendation
  [70:4:1.0] 5th (1969) | Special Category Status introduced (Mahavir Tyagi); funds by the Gadgil formula (NDC)
  [70:4:1.1] 9th | Calamity Relief Fund (from 1990)
  [70:4:1.2] 10th | Local bodies: ₹100 per capita of rural population (1971 Census) for Panchayats
  [70:4:1.3] 13th | National Disaster Response Reserve (NDRR), ₹250 crore; NCCF merged into the NDRF
  [70:4:1.4] 14th | Tax devolution over grants; 42%
  [70:4:1.5] 16th | Revenue-deficit grants ended; 3% GSDP deficit cap; GDP contribution criterion
[70:4:2] - Grants under **Art. 275** are for needy States; the FC does not decide **Plan** transfers.
[70:4:3] # Special Category Status
[70:4:4] - First States: **Assam, Jammu & Kashmir, Nagaland**; criteria: **hilly terrain**, low density or large **tribal** share, **strategic border**, economic and infrastructure **backwardness** (not high income).
[70:4:5] # Andhra Pradesh
[70:4:6] TABLE head: FC | AP's share of the States' pool
  [70:4:6.0] 13th | for undivided AP – apportioned between AP and Telangana on population ratio (AP Reorganisation Act, 2014)
  [70:4:6.1] 14th (2015–20) | 4.305%
  [70:4:6.2] 15th (2021–26) | 4.047% (≈4.05%)
  [70:4:6.3] 16th (2026–31) | 4.217% (≈4.22%)
[70:4:7] - AP's share **fell** from the 14th to the 15th FC and **rose** under the 16th (still below the 14th).
[70:4:8] - **SCS for AP**: **promised in Parliament in 2014**, **not** in the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014; the Centre gave a **special assistance** measure instead.
[70:4:9] - 16th FC grants to AP: rural local bodies **₹16,627 crore**, urban **₹12,158 crore**, disaster **₹6,125 crore**; **Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam** eligible for up to **₹5,000 crore each** for **wastewater** systems.
[70:4:10] - AP memorandum (Feb 2026): higher vertical devolution + criteria for **capital-city and infrastructure** costs from post-bifurcation imbalances.
[70:4:11] - AP Finance Minister: AP lost up to **₹38,000 crore** when revenue-deficit grants were dropped; AP Budget 2026-27 revenue deficit **1.1%**.
[70:4:12] - Aug 2026: ULB elections for **100 of 123** ULBs – only duly constituted ULBs can draw 16th FC grants.
[70:4:13] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.46; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 26 p.11; AP Budget 2026-27 speech; app's current notes (row 70); 13th FC report ch.11 (disaster relief)
## SUB 5 | 15th and 16th Finance Commissions – Devolution Formula
[70:5:0] # 15th Finance Commission (2020–26)
[70:5:1] - Formed **27 November 2017**; Chairman **N.K. Singh**; **first FC to cut** the vertical share: **42% → 41%**, because of the change in **J&K's status** (2019).
[70:5:2] - Used **2011 population** only; **added demographic performance and tax effort**.
[70:5:3] - Local-body grants **₹4.36 lakh crore** (urban share 36%).
[70:5:4] # 16th Finance Commission (2026–31)
[70:5:5] - Constituted **31 December 2023**; Chairman **Arvind Panagariya**; members **T. Rabi Sankar, Annie George Mathew, Manoj Panda, Soumya Kanti Ghosh**; award **2026-27 to 2030-31**.
[70:5:6] - Terms of reference taken straight from the **Constitution**; population base 2011 (demographic performance measured against 1971).
[70:5:7] - Report to the President **17 November 2025**; tabled in Parliament **1 February 2026** (Budget day); devolution accepted in the **Budget 2026-27**; **41%** of the divisible pool retained; total transfers **₹25.44 lakh crore** for 2026-27.
[70:5:8] - Total grants **₹9.47 lakh crore**; **revenue-deficit grants discontinued**; **Kerala** got neither revenue-deficit nor State-specific grants.
[70:5:9] - **Local-body grants ₹7.91 lakh crore**: rural ~**₹4.35 lakh crore**, urban ~**₹3.56 lakh crore** (= **45%**); urbanisation premium ₹10,000 crore.
[70:5:10] - **Disaster corpus ₹2.04 lakh crore**; sharing **90:10** NE/Himalayan States, **75:25** others; **heatwaves and lightning** proposed as new notified disasters.
[70:5:11] - **State deficits capped at 3% of GSDP**.
[70:5:12] - All five **southern States** gained: Karnataka **4.131%** (15th 3.64%), Tamil Nadu **4.097%**; southern States still call population and income distance criteria unfair.
[70:5:13] TABLE head: Criterion (horizontal) | 15th FC | 16th FC
  [70:5:13.0] Income distance | 45 | 42.5 (highest)
  [70:5:13.1] Population (2011) | 15 | 17.5
  [70:5:13.2] Area | 15 | 10
  [70:5:13.3] Forest and ecology | 10 | 10 (incl. open forests)
  [70:5:13.4] Demographic performance | 12.5 | 10
  [70:5:13.5] Tax and fiscal effort | 2.5 | dropped
  [70:5:13.6] Contribution to GDP | – | 10 (new, first time)
[70:5:14] - **Vertical devolution** = Centre ↔ States (share of the pool); **horizontal** = among States (criteria and weights).
[70:5:15] - Number game: 32 → 42 → 41 → 41 (13th → 14th → 15th → 16th).
[70:5:16] ~~ Sources: Union Budget 2026-27 speech para 91; Praveen CA360 Feb 2026; PMF Lens Feb 2026; NextGen Indian Economy P1 - APPSC 01; app's current notes (row 70)

  Recommending the distribution of divisible Union taxes between the Centre and States | Recommending the allocation of the States' share among the States | Recommending principles for grants-in-aid out of the Consolidated Fund of India | *Resolving Centre-State legal disputes under Article 131
  x: Article 131 disputes go to the Supreme Court; the other three are Finance Commission functions.

=== NOTES 2:71 | Comptroller and Auditor General – Appointment, Duties, Types of Audit, Audit Reports and Pac Linkage
## SUB 0 | CAG – Status, Appointment, Term and Removal
[71:0:0] # Status
[71:0:1] - Official name: **Comptroller and Auditor-General of India**; **Part V, Chapter V**, Articles **148–151** – an **independent constitutional authority created by the Constitution** (Art. 148), not by an Act, a Cabinet resolution or under the Finance Ministry.
[71:0:2] TABLE head: Article | Content
  [71:0:2.0] 148 | Appointment, oath, term, removal; 148(4) post-retirement bar; 148(6) expenses charged
  [71:0:2.1] 149 | Duties and powers (Parliament prescribes them – CAG Act, 1971)
  [71:0:2.2] 150 | Form of accounts – prescribed by the President on the CAG's advice
  [71:0:2.3] 151 | Audit reports: Union → President (151(1)); State → Governor (151(2))
[71:0:3] - Head of the **Indian Audit and Accounts Department**; "**Guardian of the Public Purse**" / of public finance.
[71:0:4] - **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**: the CAG is "the **most important officer** under the Constitution"; one of the bulwarks of democracy with the **Supreme Court, Election Commission and UPSC**; auditing both Union and State accounts is a **unitary** feature.
[71:0:5] - The CAG is **not part of the Union Executive** (President, VP, PM, Council of Ministers, Attorney General), nor is the **Speaker** (part of Parliament).
[71:0:6] - For the President's election, **CAG** is an **office of profit**; the posts of VP, Governor and Minister are not (Art. 58 explanation).
[71:0:7] - **Table of Precedence:** CAG is at **9A** with the **Chairperson UPSC** and the **Chief Election Commissioner**; Chief Justices of High Courts are at 14.
[71:0:8] # Appointment, term and removal
[71:0:9] - Appointed by the **President** by **warrant under his hand and seal** (Art. 148(1)) – not the PM, FM, UPSC, Parliament or a PM–LoP committee; Attorney General (Art. 76) and Governor (Art. 155) are also appointed by the President.
[71:0:10] - **Oath** before the **President** (or a person he appoints); form in the **Third Schedule**.
[71:0:11] - **Term: 6 years or age 65, whichever is earlier** (CAG Act, 1971) – the longest among President, VP and Lok Sabha member (5 years). Same as **CEC/ECs and UPSC members**; SPSC members 6 years or **62**; **SC judge retires at 65**, **HC judge at 62** (15th Amendment, 1963: 60 → 62).
[71:0:12] - **Removal** in like manner and on like grounds as a **Supreme Court judge** (Art. 148(1) with Art. 124(4)): by the President on an **address by both Houses** with **special majority** for **proved misbehaviour or incapacity** – he does **not** hold office at the President's pleasure; resigns to the President.
[71:0:13] - **Constitution prescribes no qualifications** for the CAG; it is a **single-member** office.
[71:0:14] # Persons
[71:0:15] TABLE head: CAG | Fact
  [71:0:15.0] V. Narahari Rao | First CAG of independent India (from 15 August 1948)
  [71:0:15.1] A.K. Chanda | 3rd CAG (later 3rd FC Chairman)
  [71:0:15.2] Vinod Rai | 11th CAG, Jan 2008 – May 2013 (2G report; wrote "When Audit Matters")
  [71:0:15.3] Shashi Kant Sharma | 2013–17
  [71:0:15.4] Rajiv Mehrishi | Sept 2017 – Aug 2020
  [71:0:15.5] Girish Chandra Murmu | 2020–24
  [71:0:15.6] K. Sanjay Murthy | 15th CAG, since 21 November 2024 (as of 2026)
[71:0:16] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 20 p.11, 27 p.4; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.52 p.632-638, App. III Table of Precedence; app's current notes (row 71)
## SUB 1 | Audit Reports, PAC and Parliamentary Control
[71:1:0] # Report to action
[71:1:1] - **CAG report → President (Union) / Governor (State)** under **Art. 151** → laid before **Parliament / State Legislature** → examined by the **Public Accounts Committee** (PSUs: **Committee on Public Undertakings**) → **Action Taken Notes**.
[71:1:2] - Reports go first to the **President**, not to the PAC, the Speaker, the PM, the CJI or the Vice-President; State reports to the **Governor** (Art. **151(2)**).
[71:1:3] - Three Union reports: **Appropriation Accounts, Finance Accounts, Public Undertakings** (not Estimates).
[71:1:4] - **Ultimate action** on CAG reports rests with **Parliament** (not the President, SC or NDC).
[71:1:5] - **Art. 281/151/338:** the President must lay before Parliament the **FC recommendations**, the **CAG report** and the **NCSC report** – the **PAC report** is not laid by him (it goes to the Speaker).
[71:1:6] # Public Accounts Committee
[71:1:7] - Set up **1921** (GoI Act, 1919); **22 members (15 LS + 7 RS)**, elected yearly by **single transferable vote**; **no Minister**.
[71:1:8] - Chairman appointed by the **Speaker**, from the **Opposition since 1967**; 2026-27 chair **K.C. Venugopal**; PAC reports to the **Speaker** / Parliament.
[71:1:9] - Main function: **examine the CAG's audit reports** (Appropriation and Finance Accounts) – not day-to-day interference or orders.
[71:1:10] - CAG = PAC's "**friend, philosopher and guide**" – he **attends its meetings** (not the AG or Solicitor General); not of the Estimates Committee or COPU.
[71:1:11] - PAC recommendations are **not binding**; backlog of Action Taken Notes (May 2026).
[71:1:12] # CAG and Parliament
[71:1:13] - **No Minister represents the CAG** in Parliament (not the Finance Minister).
[71:1:14] - The CAG has **no right to speak, take part or vote** in either House or a joint sitting – these Art. 88 rights (speak and take part, **no vote**) belong to **Ministers and the Attorney General**.
[71:1:15] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 20 p.12, 27 p.5; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.52 p.634; app's current notes (row 71)
## SUB 2 | Duties and Powers – Article 149, 1971 Act, Types of Audit
[71:2:0] # Duties
[71:2:1] - **CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971**; **1976 amendment** (in force **1 March 1976**): **accounts separated from audit** (departmentalisation) – Union accounts now compiled by the **Controller General of Accounts** (Finance Ministry), who gives the FM a **monthly** analytical review; the CAG still keeps most **State accounts**.
[71:2:2] - Audits: expenditure from the **Consolidated Funds** of India, States and UTs with legislature; **Contingency Funds** and **Public Accounts**; trading, manufacturing, profit-and-loss accounts; **receipts** payable into the CFI; **stores and stock**.
[71:2:3] - Also **government companies** and bodies **substantially financed** by government; **local bodies** only on request of the President/Governor.
[71:2:4] - **Certifies net proceeds** of any tax or duty (incl. income tax, Art. 279) – his certificate is final; advises the President on the **form of accounts** (Art. 150).
[71:2:5] - Duty: **uphold the Constitution and laws of Parliament** in financial administration – checks not only **legality** but also **propriety** of expenditure.
[71:2:6] # Types of audit
[71:2:7] TABLE head: Type | Nature | Tests
  [71:2:7.0] Legal and regulatory (compliance) | Obligatory | Money legally available, spent as rules require
  [71:2:7.1] Financial attest | Obligatory | Accounts true
  [71:2:7.2] Propriety | Discretionary | Wisdom, faithfulness, economy; flags extravagance
  [71:2:7.3] Performance | Discretionary (2006 OM) | 3 Es: economy, efficiency, effectiveness
[71:2:8] - **Social audit**: CAG laid down the **Auditing Standards for Social Audit** of **MGNREGA** (2016).
[71:2:9] # Limits
[71:2:10] - Only an **Auditor General**, not a Comptroller: **no control over the issue of money** from the Consolidated Fund or the receipt/lodging of revenue (Britain's C&AG has it); audit is **ex-post**.
[71:2:11] - He does **not control the entire financial system of the Union only** – he audits both **Centre and States**; cannot disallow expenditure, enforce recovery, prosecute or **suo motu investigate corruption** – he only reports.
[71:2:12] - **Secret service expenditure**: accepts a **certificate** of the competent authority.
[71:2:13] TABLE head: Category | Example
  [71:2:13.0] Audited directly by CAG | DVC, ONGC
  [71:2:13.1] Private auditors on CAG's advice + CAG supplementary audit | Central Warehousing Corp., IFCI
  [71:2:13.2] Wholly private audit (no CAG role) | LIC, RBI
[71:2:14] - **Paul Appleby** criticised the CAG's role and suggested relieving it of audit.
[71:2:15] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 20 p.11-12, 27 p.4-5; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.52 p.633-636
## SUB 3 | Independence Safeguards
[71:3:0] - **Security of tenure** – removal only by the constitutional procedure.
[71:3:1] - **Salary = Supreme Court judge**, determined by Parliament – **Second Schedule (Part E)**; salary, leave, pension and retirement age **cannot be varied to his disadvantage**.
[71:3:2] - **Leave** granted or refused by the **President**.
[71:3:3] - His **salary** (Art. 112(3)) and the office's expenses (salaries, allowances, pensions of staff) are **charged on the Consolidated Fund of India** – non-votable (Art. 148(6)); the Attorney General's and Service Chiefs' salaries are not charged.
[71:3:4] - **Complete bar** on further office under GoI or any State after retirement (Art. 148(4)) – the UPSC Chairman is also barred; retired judges often head commissions.
[71:3:5] - Service conditions of IA&AD staff and his administrative powers are prescribed by the President **after consulting the CAG**.
[71:3:6] - **Not** a safeguard: holding office during the President's pleasure.
[71:3:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 20 p.11, 27 p.4; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.52 p.632-633
## SUB 4 | AP Angle, Landmark Reports and Latest
[71:4:0] - AP's audit reports go to the **Governor of AP** (Art. 151(2)); after 2014, reports on undivided AP went to the Governors of both **AP and Telangana**.
[71:4:1] - CAG State Finances, **AP 2015-16**: State's **own tax revenue ≈ 45%** of total revenue receipts.
[71:4:2] - CAG State Finances report **2022-23**: revenue receipts **₹1,57,768 crore**; own tax revenue **₹78,026 crore** (about **half**); own tax 5.92% and central transfers 5.64% of GSDP.
[71:4:3] TABLE head: Report | Fact
  [71:4:3.0] 2G spectrum (2010) | Presumptive loss ₹1.76 lakh crore
  [71:4:3.1] Coal blocks (2012) | ₹1.86 lakh crore
  [71:4:3.2] Rafale (2019) | Redacted pricing
[71:4:4] - Debate: the "**presumptive loss**" method.
[71:4:5] - **18 Sep 2026**: CAG Report No. 31 of 2026 – bio-toilets faulty at **491 of 512** stations; PAC (K.C. Venugopal) pulled up the Railways.
[71:4:6] - CAG auditing **101 cities** for ease of living; **AI/ML**-based audits to detect welfare fraud; remote audits (Sep 2025).

=== NOTES 2:72 | Attorney General and Advocate General; Solicitor General
## SUB 0 | Attorney General – Highest Law Officer, Appointment and Qualification (Art. 76)
[72:0:0] # The office
[72:0:1] - **Attorney General (AG) of India** = the **highest law officer** of the country and the **first law officer / chief legal adviser** of the **Government of India** (Art. 76).
[72:0:2]   - Distractors: the **Chief Justice of India** heads the judiciary, the **Law Minister** looks after legal matters in the Cabinet, the **Solicitor General** is only the **second** law officer, the CAG is the auditor.
[72:0:3] - **Part V** (The Union, Chapter I – The Executive); the AG is part of the **Union Executive** but **not a member of the Union Cabinet**.
[72:0:4] - **Only the AG** (Union) and the **Advocate General** (State) are constitutional law officers; the **Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General are not mentioned in Art. 76**.
[72:0:5] # Appointment and qualification – Art. 76(1)
[72:0:6] - Appointed by the **President** (on the advice of the Union Cabinet) – **not** by the PM, the CJI or "after consulting the Vice-President".
[72:0:7] - Must be **qualified to be appointed a judge of the Supreme Court** – not merely a High Court judge, "any advocate" or "a retired SC judge".
[72:0:8] TABLE head: SC-judge qualification (Art. 124(3)) = AG qualification
  [72:0:8.0] Citizen of India, and
  [72:0:8.1] (a) a High Court judge for 5 years, or
  [72:0:8.2] (b) an advocate of a High Court for 10 years, or
  [72:0:8.3] (c) a distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President
[72:0:9] - **Advocate General** (State) needs only the **High Court-judge** qualification (Art. 165(1)).
[72:0:10] > Asked as: "highest / first law officer of India" (about 10 PYQs – APPSC, SSC, UPPSC); who appoints the AG (President); the qualification (SC judge – APPSC Panchayat Secretary 2017, Hostel Welfare Officer 2017, MPPSC 2024); Art. 76(1).
[72:0:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity APPSC Part 13 (src/polity/nextgen-polity-appsc-20.txt) p.9-10; Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch53 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.188-190; app notes 2:72 sub 0-1
## SUB 1 | Attorney General – Rights in Parliament and in the Courts
[72:1:0] # Parliament – Art. 88
[72:1:1] - The AG has the right to **speak and otherwise take part** in the proceedings of **both Houses**, their **joint sitting** and **any parliamentary committee of which he is named a member** – **without being an MP**.
[72:1:2] - He **cannot vote** (UPSC 2013: "take part, be a committee member, speak" correct; "vote" wrong).
[72:1:3] - **Art. 105(4)**: he enjoys the **privileges and immunities of an MP**.
[72:1:4] - **Only the AG** among the listed officers has this right: **not** the Solicitor General, CJI, CEC, CAG, Finance Commission chairman, NHRC chairman or National Security Adviser.
[72:1:5]   - Ministers also speak in both Houses (Art. 88), so "AG and SG are the only officers allowed to participate in Parliament" is **wrong** on both counts (UPSC 2022).
[72:1:6] # Courts – Art. 76(3)
[72:1:7] - **Right of audience in all courts in the territory of India** – not only the Supreme Court, not only High Courts or Sessions courts.
[72:1:8] - The President has assigned him to **appear for the Government of India in all Supreme Court cases** in which it is concerned, to represent it in **Art. 143** references, and to appear in any High Court when required.
[72:1:9] > Asked as: which non-member can take part in Lok Sabha / Parliament (AG – 9 PYQs: UPPSC 1991-2011, Chhattisgarh 2003, Uttarakhand 2021, APPSC AE 2017); Art. 88 (APSLPRB SI 2023); right of audience in "any court of law within the territory of India" (APPSC AEE 2011, Sachivalayam).
[72:1:10] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity APPSC Part 13 (src/polity/nextgen-polity-appsc-20.txt) p.10; Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch53 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.188-190; app notes 2:72 sub 3
## SUB 2 | Attorney General – Term, Remuneration, Duties and Limitations
[72:2:0] # Term and removal – Art. 76(4)
[72:2:1] - **No fixed term** in the Constitution; **no grounds or procedure for removal**; holds office **during the pleasure of the President** – not the PM, not Parliament. So "the President cannot remove the AG" is **wrong**.
[72:2:2] - **Resigns** to the **President**; **by convention** (not by the Constitution) he resigns when the Council of Ministers resigns or is replaced (UPSC 2022: "the Constitution requires him to resign with the government" = wrong).
[72:2:3] - **Remuneration**: "such remuneration as the **President** may determine" – **not Parliament**, not fixed by the Constitution, not charged on the Consolidated Fund.
[72:2:4] # Duties – Art. 76(2)
[72:2:5] - 1. **Advise the Government of India** on legal matters **referred by the President**.
[72:2:6] - 2. Perform other duties of a legal character **assigned by the President**.
[72:2:7] - 3. Discharge functions conferred by the Constitution or any law.
[72:2:8] - References reach him through the **Ministry of Law and Justice (Department of Legal Affairs)** – only legal matters of real importance.
[72:2:9] - He does **not** preside over joint sittings of Parliament.
[72:2:10] # Limitations
[72:2:11] - Should **not advise or hold a brief against the Government of India**, nor in cases where he must advise or appear for it.
[72:2:12] - Should **not defend accused persons** in criminal prosecutions, or become a company director, **without the permission of the Government of India**.
[72:2:13] - **Not a full-time counsel** and **not a government servant**, so **not debarred from private practice**.
[72:2:14] TABLE head: Statement (APPSC Group-II Mains 2025 / UPPSC 2020) | True?
  [72:2:14.0] Appointed by the President; qualified to be an SC judge | True
  [72:2:14.1] Right of audience in all courts in India | True
  [72:2:14.2] Holds office during the pleasure of the Prime Minister / Parliament | False – President
  [72:2:14.3] Remuneration determined by Parliament | False – President
[72:2:15] > Asked as: statements on the AG (Group-II Mains 2025 "only I and II"; UPPSC 2020 "only I"); "holds office during the pleasure of the Parliament" = the wrong one (APPSC Welfare Officers Mains); who holds office during the President's pleasure (AG, not CAG/CEC/Speaker – UPPSC 2016); "President cannot remove the AG" = wrong (APPSC 2011).
[72:2:16] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch53 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.188-189; NextGen Polity APPSC Part 13 (src/polity/nextgen-polity-appsc-20.txt) p.10; app notes 2:72 sub 1-3
## SUB 3 | Advocate General of the State – Article 165
[72:3:0] # Office and appointment
[72:3:1] - **Highest (first) law officer of the State** and its **official legal adviser** – the State counterpart of the AG (Art. 76). Not the Government Pleader, Standing Counsel or Amicus Curiae.
[72:3:2] - **Part VI** (The States). Appointed by the **Governor** (Art. 165(1)) – **not the President** "on the Governor's recommendation", not the CM or Law Minister (UPSC 2009: statement false).
[72:3:3] - Qualification: **qualified to be a High Court judge** – citizen + **10 years in a judicial office** or **10 years as a High Court advocate** (no "jurist" route) – not Vidhan Sabha / Lok Sabha membership, not a magistrate.
[72:3:4] - **Pleasure of the Governor** (Art. 165(3)) – not the CM or State Cabinet; no fixed term; by convention resigns with the State government.
[72:3:5] - **Remuneration determined by the Governor** – not equal to an HC judge, Chief Secretary or State minister (APPSC Group-II Prelims 2017).
[72:3:6] # Duties and rights
[72:3:7] - **Art. 165(2)**: advise the **State Government** on legal matters referred by the Governor and perform other legal duties assigned.
[72:3:8] - **Art. 177**: may speak and take part in **either House of the State Legislature** and its committees – **no vote**; **Art. 194(4)**: privileges of a member of the State Legislature.
[72:3:9] - Right of audience: in courts **in the State** (the AG: all courts in India).
[72:3:10] - **Not appointed by the Governor:** **High Court judges** (the **President** appoints them, Art. 217); the Governor does appoint the CM, the Advocate General and the SPSC chairman.
[72:3:11] - **AP:** the Advocate General of AP is appointed by the **Governor of AP**; **Dammalapati Srinivas** was reappointed on **19 June 2024**. The Advocate General may use the **multi-colour AP State emblem** (G.O. of 14 Nov 2018).
[72:3:12] > Asked as: who appoints the Advocate General (Governor – 4 PYQs); legal adviser to the State Government (Advocate General – UPPSC 2014, UP Lower 2015); qualification (HC judge); remuneration (Governor); "which is not appointed by the Governor" (HC judge – APSLPRB 2017).
[72:3:13] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity APPSC Part 10.2 (src/polity/nextgen-polity-appsc-17.txt) p.14-15; Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch54 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.191-193; app notes 2:72 sub 5-6
## SUB 4 | Solicitor General and the Office-holders
[72:4:0] # Solicitor General (SG) and ASGs
[72:4:1] - **SG = second law officer** of India; **assists the AG**; is himself assisted by **Additional Solicitors General**.
[72:4:2] - He is a **legal adviser** (tenders advice and appears for the Union) – not an administrative officer, not the President's personal law officer.
[72:4:3] - **Statutory, not constitutional** – **Law Officers (Terms and Conditions) Rules, 1987**; appointed by the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet**; normal term **3 years**.
[72:4:4] - **No Art. 88 right** to take part in Parliament.
[72:4:5] - **AG and SG** are **ex officio members of the Bar Council of India** (**Advocates Act, 1961**).
[72:4:6] # Office-holders
[72:4:7] TABLE head: Office | First | Later / current (as of Nov 2026)
  [72:4:7.0] Attorney General | M.C. Setalvad (1950-63) | Soli J. Sorabjee 1998-2004; Mukul Rohatgi 2014-17; K.K. Venugopal 1 Jul 2017 – 30 Sep 2022; R. Venkataramani (16th AG) from 1 Oct 2022, extended Oct 2025
  [72:4:7.1] Solicitor General | C.K. Daphtary | Tushar Mehta (from 2018; reappointed for 3 years from 1 July 2026)
[72:4:8] - **K.K. Venugopal** = AG of the **2017-2022** period (APPSC FRO 2022 key); "the current AG is Mukul Rohatgi" was wrong in 2018 (AG then: Venugopal).
[72:4:9] - **Soli Sorabjee** = AG when Uttarakhand PCS (Mains) 2002 asked (also AG 1989-90).
[72:4:10] > Asked as: SG is "a legal adviser" (UPPSC 1991, 1994); current AG at the time of the exam (Sorabjee 2002; Venugopal 2018-2023 papers; not Rohatgi) – check the year, these keys age.
[72:4:11] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch53 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.189; app notes 2:72 sub 4, 7-8; lawmin.gov.in / PIB (law officers' appointments, 2022, 2025, 2026)

=== NOTES 2:73 | National Commission for SCs (338), STs (338A) and Backward Classes (338B); Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (350B)
## SUB 0 | Articles and Amendments – 338, 338A, 338B, 350B
[73:0:0] TABLE head: Body | Article | Created / changed by
  [73:0:0.0] Special Officer (Commissioner) for SCs and STs | 338 (original) | Constitution, 1950
  [73:0:0.1] Combined National Commission for SCs and STs | 338 | 65th Amendment, 1990 (in force 12 Mar 1992)
  [73:0:0.2] NCSC (separate) | 338 | 89th Amendment, 2003 (bifurcation); from 2004
  [73:0:0.3] NCST | 338A | 89th Amendment, 2003; came into being 19 Feb 2004
  [73:0:0.4] NCBC | 338B | 102nd Amendment, 2018 (statutory from 1993)
  [73:0:0.5] Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities | 350B | 7th Amendment, 1956
[73:0:1] - **Constitutional bodies** "in the sense that they are directly established by the Constitution": NCSC (338), NCST (338A), NCBC (338B, since 2018), Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (350B). **NCW, NCM, NHRC, NCPCR are statutory.**
[73:0:2]   - So NCST was created by a **constitutional amendment** – not a government order, Cabinet resolution or statute.
[73:0:3] - **Distractors:** Art. **340** = Backward Classes Commission (Kalelkar, Mandal); **341/342** = lists of SCs/STs; **280** = Finance Commission; **332** = Assembly seats for SCs/STs; **350** = representation for grievances; **343/347** = official language.
[73:0:4] - Evolution: 1978 non-statutory Commission for SCs and STs (resolution) → **1987** resolution renamed it the National Commission → **65th Amendment** replaced the single Special Officer with a multi-member constitutional body → **1999** Ministry of Tribal Affairs → **89th** split it.
[73:0:5] - **102nd Amendment** also inserted **Art. 342A** (President notifies SEBCs) and relieved the **NCSC of backward-class work**; the **105th Amendment (2021)** restored States' power to keep their own SEBC lists.
[73:0:6] - **⚠ Dated key:** before 2018 the NCBC was statutory, so old papers answer "NCBC is not a constitutional body"; today all four (NCSC, NCST, NCBC, Special Officer) are constitutional.
[73:0:7] > Asked as: Article for NCSC (338 – 6 PYQs), NCST (338A – 4), Special Officer (350B); amendment that created NCST / split the commission (89th – 3); NCBC status (102nd – APPSC FRO 2022); odd one out "not a constitutional body".
[73:0:8] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity APPSC Part 13 (src/polity/nextgen-polity-appsc-20.txt) p.12-14; Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch48-50 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.169-176; app notes 2:73 sub 0, 4, 7
## SUB 1 | Composition, Functions, Powers and Reports
[73:1:0] # Composition
[73:1:1] - NCSC, NCST and the constitutional NCBC each: **Chairperson + Vice-Chairperson + 3 other members**.
[73:1:2] - Appointed by the **President by warrant under his hand and seal**; tenure fixed by the President's Rules (2004) = **3 years**; not more than **two terms**.
[73:1:3] - The statutory NCBC (1993 Act, in force 2 Apr 1993) had **5 members** headed by a **retired judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court**.
[73:1:4] # Functions (Art. 338(5), 338A(5), 338B(5))
[73:1:5] - 1. **Investigate and monitor** the constitutional and legal safeguards and evaluate their working.
[73:1:6] - 2. **Inquire into specific complaints** of deprivation of rights and safeguards.
[73:1:7] - 3. **Participate and advise on the planning process** of socio-economic development and evaluate progress.
[73:1:8] - 4. **Present reports to the President** annually (and when it deems fit) – **not to the Prime Minister**; the President lays them before **Parliament** with an action-taken memorandum; State-related reports go to the **Governor** (NCBC: to the State government).
[73:1:9] - 5. Recommend measures for effective implementation of safeguards.
[73:1:10] - **Not** functions: giving scholarships, raising a protection force, implementing Union welfare schemes, punishing offenders.
[73:1:11] - **Consultation:** the Union and every State must consult the Commission on all major policy matters (Art. 338(9), 338A(9)); proposals for **de-reservation** of posts are examined by the NCSC/NCST/NCBC first (NCSC review of three years' proposals, Aug 2026).
[73:1:12] - **NCST extra (2005 Rules):** ownership of **minor forest produce**, rights over mineral and water resources, rehabilitation of displaced tribals, PESA implementation.
[73:1:13] # Powers – Art. 338(8)
[73:1:14] - While investigating or inquiring it has **all the powers of a civil court trying a suit**: **summon** and examine on oath; **discovery of documents**; **receive evidence on affidavits**; **requisition any public record** from any court or office; **issue summons** for examining witnesses and documents. It **cannot punish**; its advice is recommendatory.
[73:1:15] > Asked as: NCST tenure (3 years) and members besides Chairperson and Vice (3); a function of NCSC (advise on planning); NOT a function (report to the PM – APPSC Group-I); civil-court powers "all of the above" (APPSC Group-I 2023).
[73:1:16] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch48-50 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.169-176; NextGen Polity APPSC Part 13 (src/polity/nextgen-polity-appsc-20.txt) p.13-14; app notes 2:73 sub 1-3

  [73:2:0.1] NCSC (2004) | Suraj Bhan | Kishor Makwana (from Mar 2024)

  [73:2:0.4] NCM | Justice Mohd. Sardar Ali Khan (1993) | Harjit Singh Grewal (Jul 2026)

## SUB 3 | Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities – Art. 350B
[73:3:0] - **Art. 350B** inserted by the **7th Amendment, 1956** (with **Art. 350A**) on the **States Reorganisation Commission's** recommendation – not the 9th Amendment.
[73:3:1] - **One** Special Officer for the whole country, **appointed by the President** – there is **no** post "for every State".
[73:3:2] - Duty: **investigate all matters relating to the safeguards** for linguistic minorities and **report to the President**, who lays the reports before **each House of Parliament** and sends them to the States.
[73:3:3] - Office created **1957**; designated **Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities (CLM)**; under the **Ministry of Minority Affairs**; headquarters **New Delhi** (moved back from Allahabad, 2015); regional offices **Belgaum, Chennai, Kolkata**.
[73:3:4] - The Constitution does **not** fix his qualifications, tenure, salary or removal.
[73:3:5] - **Art. 350A**: States to provide **instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage** to linguistic-minority children.
[73:3:6] > Asked as: Article for the Special Officer (350B – APPSC FRO 2022); statements "one officer for every State" and "added by the 9th Amendment" both false (UPPSC 2024).
[73:3:7] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch51 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.177-179; app notes 2:73 sub 6
## SUB 4 | Backward Classes Commissions, Other Bodies and the AP Angle
[73:4:0] # Backward Classes Commissions (Art. 340)
[73:4:1] TABLE head: Commission | Chairman | Year | Government
  [73:4:1.0] First Backward Classes Commission | Kaka Kalelkar | 29 Jan 1953 | Nehru
  [73:4:1.1] Second Backward Classes Commission | B.P. Mandal | 1 Jan 1979 | Janata (Morarji Desai)
[73:4:2] - **Mandal** first recommended **27%** OBC reservation; **Indra Sawhney v UoI (16 Nov 1992)** upheld 27%, the **creamy layer**, and ordered a permanent body → statutory **NCBC (1993 Act)**.
[73:4:3] - First reservation policy: **Kolhapur (Shahu Maharaj), 1902**; Art. 15(4) added by the **1st Amendment, 1951**.
[73:4:4] # Status of other bodies
[73:4:5] - **NCW, NCM, NHRC** = statutory; **NITI Aayog** = executive (**Cabinet resolution**, 1 Jan 2015); **NCSK** = statutory under a **1993 Act** (lapsed 29 Feb 2004), now **non-statutory**, extended to **31 March 2028**.
[73:4:6] # AP angle
[73:4:7] - **AP State Commission for SCs and STs** created by a **2003** State Act; split later – **AP State Commission for Scheduled Tribes Act, 2020** (separate SC and ST commissions).
[73:4:8] > Asked as: own MCQs only (Kalelkar 1953, Mandal 1979, Kolhapur, NITI resolution, AP commissions); no PYQ in this row.
[73:4:9] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:73 sub 5, 7-8; Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch50 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.175-176

=== NOTES 2:74 | Statutory Bodies – Nhrc and SHRCs, National Commission for Women, Ncpcr, National Commission for Minorities
## SUB 0 | National Commission for Women (NCW)
[74:0:0] # Act and status
[74:0:1] - **Statutory**, not constitutional: **National Commission for Women Act, 1990** (in force 30 Aug 1990); Commission constituted on **31 January 1992**. Nodal ministry: **Women and Child Development**.
[74:0:2] - Recommended earlier by the **Committee on the Status of Women in India (1974)** and the National Perspective Plan for Women (1988).
[74:0:3] # Composition (Sec. 3)
[74:0:4] - **Chairperson + 5 members + a Member-Secretary**, all **nominated by the Central Government** (not the President, not elected).
[74:0:5] - Members: persons with experience in **law or legislation, trade unionism, management of an industry**, **women's voluntary organisations (incl. women activists)**, **administration, economic development, health, education or social welfare**; at least **one SC and one ST** member.
[74:0:6] - Member-Secretary: an expert in management, organisational structure or **sociological movement**, or a civil servant.
[74:0:7] - Term: **3 years** (chairperson and members).
[74:0:8] # Functions (Sec. 10) and powers
[74:0:9] - **Section 10** lists the functions: investigate safeguards for women; report to the **Central Government**; review laws and suggest amendments; **look into complaints and take suo motu notice** of deprivation of women's rights; special studies; **promotional and educational research** to ensure **due representation of women** in all spheres; inspect jails and remand homes; fund litigation.
[74:0:10] - **Powers of a civil court** while investigating; regulates its own procedure; forms committees and co-opts outsiders. It cannot impose or enforce criminal sentences.
[74:0:11] - **Mahila Jan Sunwai** = public hearing of women's grievances; **Parivarik Mahila Lok Adalat** for family disputes.
[74:0:12] # Chairpersons
[74:0:13] TABLE head: Chairperson | Tenure
  [74:0:13.0] Jayanti Patnaik (first) | 1992-95
  [74:0:13.1] Mohini Giri; Vibha Parthasarathy; Poornima Advani; Girija Vyas; Mamta Sharma | 1995-2014
  [74:0:13.2] Lalitha Kumaramangalam | Sep 2014 – Sep 2017 (so the chair in 2016)
  [74:0:13.3] Rekha Sharma | acting from Sep 2017, chairperson Aug 2018 – Aug 2024 (so the chair in 2019-2023)
  [74:0:13.4] Vijaya Rahatkar | from Oct 2024 (present, as of Nov 2026)
[74:0:14] - **V.S. Ramadevi** (Governor, acting CEC) was **never** NCW chairperson; Smriti Irani and Najma Heptulla were not either.
[74:0:15] > Asked as: Act and year (1990 / Jan 1992 – 4 PYQs); composition and nomination fields; term (3 years); Section 10; research on due representation (Group-II 2011); first chairperson (Jayanti Patnaik); "present" chairperson (Lalitha Kumaramangalam / Rekha Sharma / Vijaya Rahatkar by exam year – 5 PYQs).
[74:0:16] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity APPSC Part 13 (src/polity/nextgen-polity-appsc-20.txt) p.15; Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch59 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.235-240; ncw.nic.in (former chairpersons); app notes 2:74 sub 4, 9
## SUB 1 | National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)
[74:1:0] # Status
[74:1:1] - **Statutory** (not constitutional) – **Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993**; set up **12 October 1993** (ordinance of 28 Sep 1993); **Paris Principles**; headquarters **New Delhi**. Contrast: State/Union Finance Commissions (Art. 243-I, 280) and the Lok Sabha Secretariat (Art. 98) are constitutional.
[74:1:2] # Composition and appointment
[74:1:3] - **Chairperson** (former **CJI or SC judge** – since 2019) + **5 full-time members** (an SC judge, an HC Chief Justice, **3** human-rights experts incl. a woman) + **7 ex officio** members (chairs of NCM, NCSC, NCST, NCW, NCBC, NCPCR, Chief Commissioner for PwD).
[74:1:4] - Appointed by the **President** on the recommendation of a **6-member committee**: **PM (head)**, **Speaker of the Lok Sabha**, **Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha**, **Leaders of the Opposition in both Houses**, **Union Home Minister**. The **Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Vice-President) is NOT** on it.
[74:1:5] - **Removal:** by the President; for misbehaviour or incapacity only after a **Supreme Court inquiry**.
[74:1:6] TABLE head: Term | Before the 2019 amendment | After PHR (Amendment) Act, 2019
  [74:1:6.0] Chairperson and members | 5 years or 70 years of age, whichever earlier | 3 years or 70 years; eligible for reappointment
[74:1:7] # Working
[74:1:8] - Recommendations **not binding**; government reports action within one month; cannot inquire into a matter **after one year**; civil-court powers.
[74:1:9] # Chairpersons
[74:1:10] TABLE head: No. | Chairperson | Tenure
  [74:1:10.0] 1 | Justice Ranganath Misra | 1993-96
  [74:1:10.1] 2-6 | M.N. Venkatachaliah, J.S. Verma, A.S. Anand, S. Rajendra Babu, K.G. Balakrishnan | 1996-2015
  [74:1:10.2] 7 | Justice H.L. Dattu | 29 Feb 2016 – 2 Dec 2020
  [74:1:10.3] 8 | Justice Arun Kumar Mishra | 2 Jun 2021 – 1 Jun 2024
  [74:1:10.4] 9 | Justice V. Ramasubramanian | from 30 Dec 2024 (present, as of Nov 2026)
[74:1:11] > Asked as: year (1993); not a constitutional body (UPPSC 2007); term (5 years or 70 before 2019 – MPPSC 2018, now 3 years); who is not on the selection committee (RS Chairman – MPPSC 2019); 7th chairperson (H.L. Dattu – APPSC AEE 2016); "current" chairman (Dattu in older papers).
[74:1:12] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch57 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.226-230, Ch58 p.233-234 (2019 Amendment); nhrc.nic.in (former chairpersons); app notes 2:74 sub 1-2, 9
## SUB 2 | State Human Rights Commission (SHRC)
[74:2:0] - Under the same **Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993**; constituted by the **State government**; inquires only into **State List and Concurrent List** matters not already before the NHRC or another statutory commission.
[74:2:1] - **Chairperson** (former Chief Justice **or judge** of a High Court – since 2019) **+ 2 members**.
[74:2:2] - **Appointed by the Governor** on the recommendation of a committee of the **Chief Minister (head)**, **Speaker**, **State Home Minister** and **Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly** (+ Council Chairman and Council LoP where a Council exists). The **Governor is not a member** of the committee; he only appoints.
[74:2:3] - **Removed only by the President**, not the Governor. Term **3 years or 70** (5 years before 2019).
[74:2:4] - **AP SHRC** functions from **Kurnool**. **Human Rights Courts** in every district (with the HC Chief Justice's concurrence).
[74:2:5] > Asked as: who is not on the SHRC recommending committee (Governor – MPPSC 2020).
[74:2:6] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch58 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.231-234; app notes 2:74 sub 3
## SUB 3 | NCPCR and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
[74:3:0] - **NCPCR**: statutory – **Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005**; set up **2007** (Act in force 5 Feb 2007); under **Women and Child Development**; **Chairperson + 6 members** (at least 2 women); 3 years, max two terms; age limit 65 (chair) / 60 (members); State Commissions (SCPCRs) too.
[74:3:1] - Monitors the **RTE Act 2009** (incl. **Sec. 12(1)(c)** 25% free seats), **POCSO Act 2012** and **JJ Act 2015**.
[74:3:2] - "Child rights" include those in the **UNCRC**: adopted by the UN on **20 Nov 1989**, **entered into force 2 Sep 1990**, **54 articles**; **India acceded/ratified 11 Dec 1992**; a child = below **18 years**.
[74:3:3] TABLE head: Document | Year
  [74:3:3.0] UDHR | 1948 (10 Dec)
  [74:3:3.1] CEDAW | 1979
  [74:3:3.2] Convention against Torture | 1984
  [74:3:3.3] UNCRC | 1989 (in force 1990)
[74:3:4] > Asked as: UNCRC entry into force (1990) and number of articles (54) – APPSC Extension Officer and Welfare Officer flashcards.
[74:3:5] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch60 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.241-248; UNICEF / OHCHR (CRC: 54 articles, entry into force 2 Sep 1990); app notes 2:74 sub 5
## SUB 4 | National Commission for Minorities and National Commission for Safai Karamcharis
[74:4:0] # NCM
[74:4:1] - **Minorities Commission** set up by an MHA **resolution, 1978**; statutory under the **NCM Act, 1992**; first statutory Commission **1993**; under the **Ministry of Minority Affairs**.
[74:4:2] - **Chairperson + Vice-Chairperson (added 1995) + 5 members = 7**, nominated by the **Central Government**; five incl. the chair from minority communities; 3 years.
[74:4:3] - **Six notified minorities:** Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis (1993) and **Jains (27 Jan 2014)**.
[74:4:4] - **15 States** (incl. **AP**) have State Minorities Commissions.
[74:4:5] # NCSK
[74:4:6] - Constituted **1994** under the **NCSK Act, 1993**; Act lapsed **29 Feb 2004** → **non-statutory** body under the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment** (not WCD); monitors the **Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act, 2013**.
[74:4:7] - **January 2022:** the Cabinet extended it by **three years** beyond 31 Mar 2022, to **31 March 2025**; latest extension up to **31 March 2028**.
[74:4:8] - Functions: recommend programmes, **study and evaluate the implementation of schemes**, **investigate complaints** of non-implementation and **take suo motu notice** – it does **not distribute relief amounts**.
[74:4:9] > Asked as: NCSK extension of Jan 2022 (three years – APPSC); NOT a function of NCSK (distribution of relief – APPSC Welfare Officers).
[74:4:10] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch61 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.249-250; NextGen Polity APPSC Part 13 (src/polity/nextgen-polity-appsc-20.txt) p.14; PIB 19 Jan 2022 (NCSK extension); app notes 2:74 sub 6-7
## SUB 5 | Andhra Pradesh State Commissions
[74:5:0] TABLE head: AP body | Act / basis | Feature
  [74:5:0.0] AP SHRC | PHR Act, 1993 | Kurnool
  [74:5:0.1] AP Commission for BCs | AP Commission for BCs Act, 1993 | Permanent body
  [74:5:0.2] AP SC/ST Commission | AP Act, 2003 | Reconstituted 2016; now separate SC and ST commissions; SC Commission chair K.S. Jawahar
  [74:5:0.3] AP State Commission for Women | AP Women's Commission Act, 1998 | Office at Mangalagiri; chair Rayapati Sailaja
[74:5:1] - State commissions under State laws report to the **Governor**/State government and are laid before the State Legislature. **Arts. 338(9) and 338A(9)** only oblige the Union and States to **consult** the national commissions.

=== NOTES 2:75 | Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 – Structure, Jurisdiction, Working; Central Vigilance Commission
## SUB 0 | State Lokayuktas – Firsts, Appointment, Reports and Jurisdiction
[75:0:0] # Firsts and chronology
[75:0:1] TABLE head: State | Fact
  [75:0:1.0] Maharashtra | FIRST to set up a Lokayukta – Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayuktas Act, 1971; came into force 25 October 1972
  [75:0:1.1] Odisha | FIRST to pass a law (1970), but the institution started only in 1983 – not the first Lokayukta
  [75:0:1.2] Bihar | 1973
  [75:0:1.3] Rajasthan | 1973
  [75:0:1.4] Uttar Pradesh | 1975
  [75:0:1.5] Madhya Pradesh | 1982
  [75:0:1.6] Andhra Pradesh | 1983
  [75:0:1.7] Karnataka | 1984 (Karnataka Lokayukta Act; own Lokayukta Police wing)
  [75:0:1.8] Assam | 1986
  [75:0:1.9] Uttarakhand | First State to pass a Lokayukta Bill in 2011 (1 November 2011)
[75:0:2] - **⚠ Trap:** a question asking which State "constituted the Lokayukta in 1971" = **Maharashtra**; Odisha = first **Act** (1970). Some keys print Orissa – wrong.
[75:0:3] - Chronology: Sweden (1809) → first Lokpal Bill (1968) → Maharashtra Lokayukta (1971) → first Lokpal (2019).
[75:0:4] - By 2013, **21 States and 1 UT (Delhi)** had Lokayuktas.
[75:0:5] # Under the 2013 Act
[75:0:6] - **Section 63**: every State to set up a **Lokayukta** by its **own State law** within **one year (365 days)** of the Act's commencement – each State has **a Lokayukta**, not a Lokpal; the States decide its contours.
[75:0:7] # Structure, appointment, tenure, report
[75:0:8] TABLE head: Structure | States
  [75:0:8.0] Lokayukta + Upa-Lokayukta | Rajasthan, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra
  [75:0:8.1] Lokayukta only | Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh
  [75:0:8.2] Officials designated "Lokpal" | Punjab, Odisha
[75:0:9] - **Appointed by the Governor**, generally after consulting the **Chief Justice of the High Court** and the **Leader of the Opposition** (not the President, CM or CJI).
[75:0:10] - Term in most States: **5 years or 65 years of age**; **Rajasthan cut the tenure from 8 to 5 years** (2019); the **Narpat Mal Lodha committee** (2014, Rajasthan Advocate General) reviewed the Rajasthan Lokayukta Act.
[75:0:11] - **Annual consolidated report to the Governor**, who lays it with an explanatory memorandum before the State Legislature (also true of UP) – not to the CM, HC Chief Justice or Speaker.
[75:0:12] - Recommendations **advisory** in most States, **binding** in some.
[75:0:13] - Weakness: no uniform law; many lack their own investigating wing and depend on the **State police / ACB**.
[75:0:14] # Jurisdiction
[75:0:15] - Looks into **administrative actions** of public servants (corruption, maladministration) – **not judicial or legislative** acts.
[75:0:16] - **Chief Minister:** included in some States (**Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh**), excluded in others (**Maharashtra**, UP, Rajasthan, Bihar, **Andhra Pradesh**).
[75:0:17] - Ministers and higher civil servants: covered almost everywhere; **MLAs** in some States; local bodies, corporations, societies in most.
[75:0:18] - **Justice N. Santosh Hegde** (Karnataka Lokayukta): **Bellary illegal iron-ore mining report (2011)** → arrest of former minister **G. Janardhana Reddy**.
[75:0:19] > Angles: first State (Maharashtra 1971, ×6), appointing/reporting authority (Governor ×4), Uttarakhand 2011 Bill, Rajasthan 8→5, Lodha committee, CM within ambit (MP & Orissa, UPSC 1995).
[75:0:20] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.66 p.727-728 (laxmikanth-indian-polity-02 p.275-276); Rocket Polity Part 1 p.5; PMF Polity Part 4 ch.63 p.29-31; app notes 2:75 sub 8
## SUB 1 | Lokpal Bill History and the 2013 Act – Dates
[75:1:0] # Bills
[75:1:1] - **First Lokpal Bill: May 1968** (introduced **9 May 1968**, 4th Lok Sabha, Indira Gandhi govt); **passed by the Lok Sabha in 1969**, **lapsed** when the Lok Sabha was dissolved before the Rajya Sabha passed it.
[75:1:2] - **⚠ Trap: 1968 = introduced; 1969 = passed by the Lok Sabha.** "First introduced" = **1968**.
[75:1:3] - Re-introduced in **1971, 1977, 1985, 1989, 1996, 1998, 2001, Aug 2011, Dec 2011** (ten attempts in all); the tenth (Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill, 2011) became the 2013 Act.
[75:1:4] TABLE head: Stage (Lokpal Bill / Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill, 2011) | Date
  [75:1:4.0] Lokpal Bill introduced in the Lok Sabha by V. Narayanasamy, Minister of State for Parliamentary Affairs (not P. Chidambaram) | 4 August 2011
  [75:1:4.1] Referred to the Standing Committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice (chair Abhishek Manu Singhvi); civil society called it "weak" | Aug–Dec 2011
  [75:1:4.2] Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill passed by the Lok Sabha; Rajya Sabha sent it to a Select Committee | 27 December 2011
[75:1:5] # The Act – dates
[75:1:6] TABLE head: Event | Date
  [75:1:6.0] Passed by the Rajya Sabha (with amendments) – first House in 2013 | 17 December 2013
  [75:1:6.1] Lok Sabha passed the amended Bill | 18 December 2013
  [75:1:6.2] President's assent | 1 January 2014
  [75:1:6.3] Came into force | 16 January 2014
  [75:1:6.4] Lokpal began functioning | 27 March 2019
[75:1:7] - **⚠ Trap:** 1 January 2014 = assent; **16 January 2014 = in force** (G2 Mains 2025).
[75:1:8] - **Statutory** body (Act of Parliament), not constitutional.
[75:1:9] - The Act also amended the **DSPE Act, 1946**: PM-led committee for the **CBI Director**; **Directorate of Prosecution** for the CBI.
[75:1:10] - Original Act: public servant declares assets and liabilities within **30 days** of entering office; **2016 amendment**: form and manner prescribed by the **Central Government**.
[75:1:11] > Angles: year/date items dominate (first Bill 1968 ×4, LS passage Dec 2011 ×3, in force 16 Jan 2014 ×3); statement item on the 2011 Bill (introduced 4 Aug 2011, Standing Committee, "weak" → 1, 3, 4).
[75:1:12] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.66 p.724-726 (laxmikanth-indian-polity-02 p.272-274); Rocket Polity Part 1 p.5, p.6; PMF Polity Part 4 ch.63 p.29; app notes 2:75 sub 1
## SUB 2 | Ombudsman Idea and Recommending Bodies
[75:2:0] # Origin
[75:2:1] - **Ombudsman** first created in **Sweden in 1809** (Scandinavia); spread to Finland 1919, Denmark 1955, Norway 1962; **New Zealand 1962** (first Commonwealth); UK Parliamentary Commissioner 1967.
[75:2:2] - **Indian versions: Lokpal** (Union) and **Lokayukta** (State) – not Lekhpal, Tehsildar or Governor.
[75:2:3] - Other models: French **Administrative Courts**; **Procurator** system in the USSR/China.
[75:2:4] - Term **"Lokpal"** coined by **Dr. L.M. Singhvi** in **1963**.
[75:2:5] - Sweden 1809 = Ombudsman; Sweden **1766** = first right-to-information law.
[75:2:6] # Committees and commissions
[75:2:7] TABLE head: Body | Chair | Recommendation
  [75:2:7.0] Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption (1962-64) | K. Santhanam | CVC (1964) and CBI – not the Lokpal
  [75:2:7.1] First ARC (1966-70) | Morarji Desai (later K. Hanumanthaiya) | Lokpal + Lokayukta, interim report "Problems of Redressal of Citizens' Grievances" (1966) – first recommended State Lokayuktas
  [75:2:7.2] Second ARC (2007) | – | Reiterated the Lokpal
[75:2:8] - ARC: Lokpal to be appointed by the President after consulting the CJI, Speaker and RS Chairman; judiciary kept outside (as in New Zealand).
[75:2:9] - **⚠ Trap:** the Rajasthan State Administrative Reforms Committee and the Second ARC are distractors for "first recommended Lokayuktas".
[75:2:10] > Angles: origin country (Sweden/Scandinavia ×3), Indian model = Lokpal, First ARC first recommended Lokayuktas (×3), ARC chair Morarji Desai.
[75:2:11] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.66 p.721-724 (laxmikanth-indian-polity-02 p.269-272); Rocket Polity Part 1 p.5; app notes 2:75 sub 0
## SUB 3 | Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta
[75:3:0] - Law: **AP Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, 1983** (amended 2007, **2024**); **Lokayukta** for higher functionaries, **Upa-Lokayukta** for the rest.
[75:3:1] - **FIRST Lokayukta of integrated AP: Justice A. Sambasiva Rao**.
[75:3:2] - **Chief Minister is outside its purview:** the Act defines "Minister" as a member **other than the Chief Minister** of the Council of Ministers; it covers **Ministers (other than the CM), MLAs** and State public servants.
[75:3:3] - **Time bar (Section 8(2))**: no complaint can be investigated after **6 years** from the date of the action complained against (Lokpal: 7 years).
[75:3:4] - **Vacancy:** when the Lokayukta's office is vacant, the **Upa-Lokayukta** performs its functions as the **Governor** directs (P. Rajani held charge in 2025).
[75:3:5] - Appointment by the **Governor** on the selection committee's recommendation; **5-year term**.
[75:3:6] - **Aug 2026**: Justice (Retd) **T. Mallikarjuna Rao** appointed by Governor **S. Abdul Nazeer** under **Section 3(1)**; **5-year term**.
[75:3:7] - **Seat**: worked from Hyderabad after bifurcation; shifted to **Kurnool** in **2021** (principal seat).
[75:3:8] - Features: **informal procedure, easy access, almost free and prompt service, independence from executive control** – it is **not an interpreter of the Constitution** (that is the judiciary).
[75:3:9] TABLE head: Body | Role in AP
  [75:3:9.0] Lokayukta / Upa-Lokayukta | Statutory ombudsman (1983 Act); inquires, recommends; reports to the Governor
  [75:3:9.1] State Vigilance Commission | From 1964, on the CVC pattern; vigilance and disciplinary advice
  [75:3:9.2] Anti-Corruption Bureau | Police agency for PC Act offences (trap and disproportionate-assets cases)
[75:3:10] > Angles: who is outside (CM), first AP Lokayukta, 6-year bar, features (not interpreter of Constitution), vacancy rule.
[75:3:11] ~~ Sources: AP Lokayukta Act 1983 s.2, s.8(2) (Lokayukta AP citizens' charter; indiacode.nic.in); Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.66 p.727; app notes 2:75 sub 9
## SUB 4 | Lokpal – Composition, Selection, Jurisdiction and People
[75:4:0] # Composition
[75:4:1] - **Chairperson + not more than 8 members**; **50% judicial**; at least **50%** from **SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women**; minimum age **45**.
[75:4:2] - Chairperson: former **CJI**, SC judge, or an eminent person with **25 years'** experience.
[75:4:3] - Term: **5 years or age 70**; **no reappointment**; cannot be an **MP or MLA**; appointed by the **President**.
[75:4:4] # Selection Committee (5)
[75:4:5] TABLE head: Member | Role
  [75:4:5.0] Prime Minister | Chair
  [75:4:5.1] Speaker of the Lok Sabha | Member
  [75:4:5.2] Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha | Member
  [75:4:5.3] CJI or an SC judge nominated by him | Member
  [75:4:5.4] Eminent jurist (nominated by the President on the others' recommendation) | Member
[75:4:6] - **Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is NOT a member**; **Search Committee** of **at least 7 persons** (half from SC/ST/OBC/minorities/women).
[75:4:7] # Jurisdiction, powers, time limits
[75:4:8] - Covers the **PM** (except international relations, security, public order, atomic energy, space; inquiry only if **two-thirds** of the full bench approves, in camera), **Ministers, MPs** (not for anything said or votes in Parliament), **Group A–D** central officials (**C and D → CVC**, which reports back), NGOs with foreign contributions **above ₹10 lakh**, public servants **posted abroad**.
[75:4:9] - **Inquiry Wing (Section 11**; preliminary inquiry into **Prevention of Corruption Act** offences) and Prosecution Wing; **superintendence over the CBI only in cases referred by the Lokpal**; attach property **even while prosecution is pending**.
[75:4:10] - Time limits: preliminary inquiry **90 days** (+90); Inquiry Wing report **60 days**; investigation **6 months + 6 months**; trial **1 year, up to 2**; complaint bar **7 years**.
[75:4:11] - **Section 17A** belongs to the **PC Act** (prior approval before probe): **22 Jan 2026** SC split verdict – **Justice B.V. Nagarathna** (unconstitutional) vs **Justice K.V. Viswanathan**.

  [75:4:13.3] Logo | Designed by Prashant Mishra (Allahabad), 2019

[75:4:15] - Complaints (Lok Sabha reply, March 2026): **2024-25 – 292** registered, 260 disposed; 2025-26 (to Feb 2026) – 389 registered.

## SUB 5 | Central Vigilance Commission and Whistle Blowers Act
[75:5:0] TABLE head: Particular | Fact
  [75:5:0.0] Origin | Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption (chair K. Santhanam, MPs + officers); set up February 1964 by executive resolution
  [75:5:0.1] Purpose | Apex body to prevent corruption in the Central Government; advises and guides central agencies on vigilance
  [75:5:0.2] Statutory status | Vineet Narain case (1997) directed it; CVC Act, 2003 – at first neither constitutional nor statutory
  [75:5:0.3] Nature | Statutory, multi-member; not constitutional
  [75:5:0.4] Composition | Central Vigilance Commissioner + not more than 2 Vigilance Commissioners
  [75:5:0.5] Term | 4 years or age 65
  [75:5:0.6] Selection (Sec 4) | PM (chair), Union Home Minister, LoP in Lok Sabha; appointment by the President
  [75:5:0.7] Over CBI | Superintendence over the CBI in PC Act cases

[75:5:2] - **Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014** (assent **9 May 2014**): **public interest disclosure** on corruption; **competent authority** for central employees = **CVC**; anonymous complaints not taken up; 7-year bar.

=== NOTES 2:76 | Central Information Commission and State Information Commissions; Cbi and Its Legal Basis
## SUB 0 | CBI – Legal Basis, Director and Units
[76:0:0] # Legal basis
[76:0:1] - **Special Police Establishment (1941)** → **Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) Act, 1946** (it constitutes the special police force = today's **CBI**) → **CBI set up 1 April 1963** by a **Ministry of Home Affairs resolution** → **CVC (1964)**.
[76:0:2] - Set up on the recommendation of the **Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption (1962-64)**.
[76:0:3] - **Neither constitutional nor statutory**: its powers come from the DSPE Act, 1946; attached office under the **Ministry of Personnel (DoPT)**.
[76:0:4] - **Founder Director: D.P. Kohli** (1963-68). Motto: **Industry, Impartiality, Integrity**; mission – to preserve values in public life and ensure the health of the national economy.
[76:0:5] - CBI = "**caged parrot**" (SC, coal allocation case 2013); **Second ARC (2007)**: new law to replace the DSPE Act.
[76:0:6] # Director
[76:0:7] - Appointed by the **Central Government** on the recommendation of a **3-member committee**: **PM, LoP in Lok Sabha (or leader of the largest opposition party), CJI or an SC judge nominated by him** – brought by the **Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013**.
[76:0:8] - Minimum tenure **2 years**, extendable **one year at a time up to 5 years** (**2021**; same for the **ED Director**).
[76:0:9] - **Director of Prosecution**: appointed on **CVC recommendation**, **2-year** term; officers of SP rank and above chosen by a **CVC-led** committee.
[76:0:10] TABLE head: Director | Period
  [76:0:10.0] D.P. Kohli | First (1963-68)
  [76:0:10.1] Ranjit Sinha | 2012-14
  [76:0:10.2] Alok Verma | Feb 2017 – Jan 2019 (exam key of 2017-18)
  [76:0:10.3] Praveen Sood | From 25 May 2023; extended to May 2025, May 2026 and again to May 2027 (as of 2026)
[76:0:11] # Vineet Narain (1997) and State consent
[76:0:12] - **Vineet Narain v Union of India (1997)**: quashed the "**Single Directive**"; gave the **CVC superintendence** over the CBI; **2-year tenure** for the Director; **CBI alone decides** whether to investigate.
[76:0:13] - **Section 6, DSPE Act**: CBI needs the State's **consent**, as **police** is **State List Entry 2**; **AP withdrew general consent Nov 2018**, restored June 2019.
[76:0:14] - **Lokpal**: superintendence over the CBI only in cases it refers.
[76:0:15] # Mandate, units and platforms
[76:0:16] - **Corruption, economic and special crimes**, mainly **Central Government and UT employees** and their PSUs; there is **no constitutional bar** on its probing economic offences.
[76:0:17] TABLE head: Unit / platform | Purpose
  [76:0:17.0] OCSAE Prevention/Investigation Unit (2019) | Online child sexual abuse and exploitation – set up by the CBI (not NIA, NCPCR or CVC)
  [76:0:17.1] BHARATPOL | Developed by the CBI; launched 7 January 2025 by Home Minister Amit Shah; real-time Interpol requests (not RAW, IB or ED)
  [76:0:17.2] Interpol | CBI is India's National Central Bureau
[76:0:18] > Angles: year 1963, founder Kohli, DSPE Act → CBI, present Director (Alok Verma then; now Praveen Sood), OCSAE, BHARATPOL, UPSC 2026 row-match (CBI–DoPT correct).
[76:0:19] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.65 (laxmikanth-indian-polity-02 p.264-268); PMF Polity Part 4 ch.62 p.25-28; Rocket Polity Part 1 p.6; India TV / Hitavada 13-14 May 2026 (Sood extension)
## SUB 1 | Status of the Bodies and Who Appoints Whom
[76:1:0] # Status
[76:1:1] TABLE head: Body | Set up | Basis
  [76:1:1.0] CBI | 1 April 1963, MHA resolution | Non-statutory; DSPE Act 1946
  [76:1:1.1] CVC | 1964, executive resolution | Statutory from CVC Act, 2003
  [76:1:1.2] CIC / SICs | 12 Oct 2005, RTI Act s.12 / s.15 | Statutory
  [76:1:1.3] NITI Aayog | 1 Jan 2015, Cabinet resolution | Non-constitutional, non-statutory
  [76:1:1.4] SHRC | Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 | Statutory
[76:1:2] - **NITI Aayog, SHRC, CVC and CIC are all NOT mentioned in the Constitution** (answer: all four).
[76:1:3] - None of the CBI, CVC or NIA prefers impeachment charges – that is done by **either House of Parliament**.
[76:1:4] # Appointing authorities
[76:1:5] TABLE head: Post | Appointed by | Committee
  [76:1:5.0] Chief Information Commissioner / ICs | President | PM, LoP in Lok Sabha, Union Cabinet Minister nominated by PM
  [76:1:5.1] State CIC / State ICs | Governor | CM, LoP in Assembly, Cabinet Minister nominated by CM (no Chief Justice)
  [76:1:5.2] Central Vigilance Commissioner | President | PM, Union Home Minister, LoP in Lok Sabha
  [76:1:5.3] CBI Director | Central Government | PM, LoP, CJI or his nominee
  [76:1:5.4] CEC and ECs (2023 Act) | President | PM, Union Cabinet Minister, LoP
[76:1:6] - **Public Information Officers** are designated by **each public authority** (Section 5) – not by the Supreme Court; first appellate authority is a senior officer of the public authority – not elected by Parliament.
[76:1:7] > Angles: correctly paired appointing authority (CIC–President, SIC–Governor), bodies not in the Constitution.

## SUB 2 | Information Commissions Under the RTI Act
[76:2:0] - **CIC** constituted **2005** under **Section 12**: CIC + up to **10** ICs; only body that can declare an organisation a "**public authority**".
[76:2:1] - **No appeal lies against the CIC's order**: its decision on a second appeal is **binding** (Sec 19(7)); it can be challenged only by **writ** (Arts 226/32) – not an appeal to the CAT, HC or SC.
[76:2:2] - **RTI (Amendment) Act, 2019**: the **Centre fixes tenure and salaries**; **2019 Rules**: term **3 years**. Earlier the State CIC's pay = **Election Commissioner's**.
[76:2:3] - **Removal of State CIC/IC (Section 17)**: by the **Governor** after a **Supreme Court** inquiry finds proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
[76:2:4] TABLE head: Section | Content
  [76:2:4.0] 5 | PIOs designated by each public authority
  [76:2:4.1] 7 | Reply in 30 days; life or liberty – 48 hours; free for BPL
  [76:2:4.2] 8(1)(j) | Personal information – DPDP Act 2023 made it an outright exemption
  [76:2:4.3] 12 | Constitution of the CIC
  [76:2:4.4] 18 | Complaints
  [76:2:4.5] 19 | First appeal; second appeal to CIC/SIC within 90 days
  [76:2:4.6] 20 | Penalty on the PIO: ₹250 per day, maximum ₹25,000
[76:2:5] - **Economic Survey 2025-26**: called for RTI Act "**re-examination**", a "**ministerial veto**".
[76:2:6] # Andhra Pradesh Information Commission
[76:2:7] - First State Chief Information Commissioner: **C.D. (Charan Das) Arha**; **second: Jannat Hussain** (from 2010, united AP).
[76:2:8] - Later: P. Ramesh Kumar (2020, residuary AP); **R. Mahaboob Basha** (2025).
[76:2:9] > Angles: appeal against CIC (none), appointing authority, second AP CIC.

## SUB 3 | Other Enforcement Agencies and the Corruption Perceptions Index

=== NOTES 2:77 | Niti Aayog – Structure, Functions, Initiatives; Contrast with the Planning Commission
## SUB 0 | Planning Commission and the National Development Council
[77:0:0] # Planning Commission
[77:0:1] - Set up **15 March 1950** by a **resolution of the Union Cabinet / Government of India** – **non-constitutional, non-statutory** (not by an amendment or ordinance); the Constitution provides for the Finance Commission (Art. 280), Election Commission (Art. 324) and UPSC (Art. 315), **not** the Planning Commission.
[77:0:2] - **First Chairman: Jawaharlal Nehru** (PM ex officio); first Deputy Chairman **Gulzarilal Nanda**; the Deputy Chairman had **Cabinet Minister** rank.
[77:0:3] - Early Five-Year Plans (from 1951, Mahalanobis model in the 2nd) gave the public sector the commanding heights and kept the **market economy at bay**.
[77:0:4] - Cabinet repealed the 1950 resolution on **13 August 2014** (Modi govt); **no longer in existence** – replaced by NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015.
[77:0:5] # National Development Council
[77:0:6] - Set up **6 August 1952** by an **executive order** – **non-constitutional and non-statutory** (calling it statutory is wrong).
[77:0:7] - Members: **PM (chairman)**, **Union Cabinet Ministers**, **Chief Ministers of all States**, CMs/administrators of UTs, members of the Planning Commission – **not** the Finance Commission Chairman or the CJI.
[77:0:8] - **Secretary: the Secretary of the Planning Commission**; meant to meet at least **twice a year**.
[77:0:9] - Role: **coordinator between the Planning Commission and the States**; **final approval of Five-Year Plans**; prescribes **guidelines** for formulating the Plan, **considers/discusses its progress**, and **suggests ways to achieve its targets** – it did not allocate plan money.
[77:0:10] - Restructured into NITI Aayog's **Governing Council**.
[77:0:11] > Angles: Planning Commission basis (Cabinet resolution ×3), first chairman, NDC date/members/secretary/functions (×8), "not in existence now".
[77:0:12] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.56 (laxmikanth-indian-polity-02 p.215-220); Rocket Polity Part 2 p.20-21; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy 10th ed. ch.5; app notes 2:77 sub 0
## SUB 1 | NITI Aayog – Status, Structure and Hubs
[77:1:0] - Came into force on **1 January 2015** (Cabinet Secretariat notification) by a **Union Cabinet resolution** – **neither constitutional nor statutory** (not an ordinance or Act); a **think-tank**; based on **cooperative federalism**.
[77:1:1] - **Chairperson: the Prime Minister** (ex officio – no full-time chairman); **Vice-Chairperson** (Cabinet rank), appointed by the PM; full-time members (MoS rank); ex-officio Union Ministers; a **CEO**.
[77:1:2] - **First Vice-Chairman: Arvind Panagariya**; then Rajiv Kumar, Suman K. Bery; **Ashok Kumar Lahiri** from April 2026 (as of 2026).
[77:1:3] - Nodal agency for **poverty estimation**.
[77:1:4] TABLE head: Body / hub | Role

## SUB 2 | NITI Aayog vs the Planning Commission
[77:2:0] TABLE head: Feature | Planning Commission | NITI Aayog
  [77:2:0.0] Approach | Top-down | Bottom-up, cooperative federalism (Team India)
  [77:2:0.1] Funds | Allocated funds to States | No fund allocation (Finance Ministry / Finance Commission)
  [77:2:0.2] States | Limited role | Equal partners
  [77:2:0.3] Basis | Cabinet resolution 1950 | Cabinet resolution 2015
[77:2:1] - NITI envisages: **empowered States as equal partners**, a **think-tank** role (domain knowledge, strategy), a **catalyst** role – but **not allocation of resources to needy States**.
[77:2:2] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.56; app notes 2:77 sub 2

## SUB 4 | NITI Aayog Initiatives – Aspirational Districts and Others
[77:4:0] TABLE head: Initiative | Launch | Coverage
  [77:4:0.0] Atal Innovation Mission | 2016 | Innovation and entrepreneurship
  [77:4:0.1] Women Entrepreneurship Platform | 2018 | Women entrepreneurs
  [77:4:0.2] Aspirational Districts (ADP) | January 2018 | 112 districts, 49 indicators, 5 themes
  [77:4:0.3] Aspirational Blocks (ABP) | Jan 2023 | 513 blocks in 329 districts (27 States, 4 UTs)
[77:4:1] - ADP themes: **Health and Nutrition 30%**, Education 30%, Agriculture and Water Resources 20%, **Financial Inclusion and Skill Development 10%**, Basic Infrastructure 10% – **Urban Transport and Housing is NOT a theme**; strategy = **Convergence, Collaboration, Competition**.
[77:4:2] - **AP**: original – **Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, YSR Kadapa**; now **Alluri Sitarama Raju, Parvathipuram Manyam, YSR Kadapa** (Kurnool, Anantapur are NOT); AP Reorganisation Act 2014 package for 7 backward districts (**4 Rayalaseema** + 3 North Coastal).
